titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: However, having said that, I still think we have to do what we need to do to defend them because the alternatives are hardly more promising.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: Or any Prime Minister.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: Well I think there's a lot of room for tough love, particularly in private and behind you know, closed doors.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: As I write in my book, you know, certainly Prime Minister Netanyahu and I have had very rigorous conversations that have gone on in person and over the phone.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: But I—I just don't think it's a particularly productive approach for the United States to take because in large measure, it opens the door to everybody else to delegitimize Israel to, you know, pile on in ways that are not good for the—the strength and stability, not just of Israel obviously but of the region.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: And so, in the absence of you know, some kind of greater goal that we were trying to achieve by doing that I just don't think that is the smartest approach.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: Yes, I would, Robin.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: And I—and I would because I think that we have to attempt to do that, you know?

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: When I first went to Oman in January of 2011, we didn't know whether any effort at some kind of secret channel would pay off.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: We still had the P5-plus-1 that was going on and we knew that eventually whatever the United States did would have to merge into the international approach.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: But we had to begin to explore it.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: And we explored it over that summer.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: That's when we had the first, you know, visit to discuss anything could be possible.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: It takes awhile, as you know so well, being such an expert in this region, to figure out who's at the table, what the conversation's about, how seriously it will be taken, who's backing you up.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: And so, then when the—the talks actually started, just in the Iranian-American channel with Bill Burns and Jake Sullivan and Bob Einhorn was also involved.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: It was—it was exploratory and it laid down some of the—the ground rules that we were looking for, and then eventually it was merged into the larger P5-plus-1 once there was a change in government in Iran and there was some real seriousness of effort.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: So with respect to the other issues, I—I—I have very clearly, in the public arena, seen the Iranians at the highest levels reject any such discussion.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: They don't want to talk about Yemen, they don't want to talk about anything other than the nuclear agreement.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: Now that was a strategic decision we made back then.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: You know, number one, it appeared to us in the early discussions with them, trying to figure out how to proceed.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: They wanted to talk about everything as a way to get some items on the table to trade off for the nuclear agreement, so that they would not have to make, perhaps, as many concessions as we were expecting them to make.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: That's why we kept very focused on just the nuclear program.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: We also had the continuing challenge, and it would be even in this instance, of our friends in the Gulf not wanting us to talk about anything that affected them in a bilateral channel with the Iranians, and you can understand why.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: I mean, they—you know, if they weren't going to be at the table, they didn't want the United States talking about Yemen or talking about anything else of interest, of vital interest in their views to them.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: So if there were a way to construct such a—a channel, I would be open to it, but I'm just laying out some of the difficulties of us being able to do that on this suite of other issues that are complex that touch many of the—the region's vital interests.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: And—and I think when it comes to Syria, we have historically not wanted to talk to Iran about Syria because we knew Iran was basically the principal supporter, propper up if you will, of Assad and we wanted to get the rest of the international community in harness to have a set of expectations and demands before we brought Iran in.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: So we have to—you know, we have to readjust this all the time.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: Just as I said, diplomacy is the balancing of risk, it's also the—the constant evaluation of where the opportunities are, where the openings are, what possibly could happen now that didn't happen before.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: So I'm open but I am very sober about how it would have to be constructed and what it would actually cover and who would have to be either at the table or you know, in the—in the first chair behind, so that they didn't feel that they were being left out or negotiated over.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: Here comes your microphone.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: So I think that's a very—it's an important questions.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: I don't know if you could hear the question.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: But it was—it was aimed at, what could you do to up the cost on Russia, for example, to be a more productive partner in seeking a solution?

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: And how would we do more to—as I understood what you said, you know, work with our European partners on these securities issues that are challenging Europe?

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: And we see that everyday with the refugees because it's humanitarian but it's also a security challenge as well?

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: Well, you know, I—I have been—I remain convinced that we need a concerted effort to really up the costs on Russia, and in particular on Putin.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: I think we have not done enough.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: I am in the category of people who wanted us to do more in response to the annexation of Crimea and the continuing destabilization of Ukraine.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: I understand the hesitation, not only in our country but most importantly, in Europe.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: The sanctions came out of the all discussions and you know, maybe to some extent they have had you know, some impact.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: I think the falling oil price has had more impact and we've got to figure out how we you know, combine both in looking at ways to put more—to up the costs, to put more pressure on Putin.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: I think it's one of the long term security challenges that United States, Europe, and especially NATO face.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: And I don't think we can dance around it very much longer.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: I mean, we all wish it wasn't the case.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: We all wish it would go away.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: We all wish that Putin would choose to modernize his country and move toward the west, instead of you know, sinking himself deeper into you know, historical roots of czar-like behavior and intimidation along borders, and projecting Russian power in places like Syria and elsewhere.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: But I think the jury is in, I think that he intends to continue to do what he is doing and go as far as he can get away with.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: And I believe that we've got to regroup—we've got to regroup quickly, because I worry very much about what's happening in Syria right now.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: Troops on the ground to allegedly protect military supplies.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: What is Russia's real objective?

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: You know, the stated objective, the public objective, to fight terrorism, has always been their rationale.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: Why did they support Assad?

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: Because after Assad there would be terrorism.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: Now, obviously if we had a different approach from the beginning working together we might've avoided this.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: We might've actually help to midwife a political transition.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: So I think we've got to spend a lot more time.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: All the—you know, all the Russian experts that you know, that thought that their work was done after the fall of the Berlin Wall, I hope that they will be dusting off their materials and I'm looking right at Strobe Talbott, and you know, get back in the game with us.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: Because, I think Russia's objectives are to stymie and to confront and to undermine American power whenever and wherever they can.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: I don't think there's much—you know, I don't think there's much to be surprised about that.So where we can work with them?

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: You know, that's one of the—you know, one of the criticisms that sometimes comes from the right, the Republicans.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: You know, \"What did the reset ever accomplish?\" Well, Medvedev was president actually quite a lot.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: We did the New START agreement.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: We got cooperation on Iran because when we got the Security Council to pass the sanctions that we had been working so hard on, that was under Medvedev in June of 2010.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: We got support to ship lethal material and equipment across to Russia to resupply our troops.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: Now, that all changed once you know, Putin announced he was going to be president again now.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: There's—I don't admire very much about Mr. Putin, but the idea you can stand and say, \"I will be your next president.\" That does have a certain, you know, attraction to it.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: So, you know, I think we've got—we've really—we are not spending the—the time.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: We're not thinking, we're not digging deep into what are we going to do.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: So, to answer the question of the—of the woman who asked, we have to do more to get back talking about how we try to confine, contain, deter Russian aggression in Europe and beyond.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: And try to figure out what are the best tools for doing that and don't lose sight of the architect because we're going to have a lot of issues up there well.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: So, I—I—I was always of that opinion.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: Expressed it vocally within the administration.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: And nothing that has happened since has in anyway persuaded me other wise.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: Well, I—I do think we're capable of doing more than one thing although sometimes it appears difficult.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: And—and I think we've got to be much more global in our thinking and globally present.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: The rebalancing to Asia, otherwise known as the pivot, was in response to the very real sense of abandonment that Asian leaders expressed to me.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: My phone calls to them before I ever went to the region in February of 2009, you know, they—they believed that because we were focused in Afghanistan and we were so focused in Iraq, and obviously had to be given all that we had invested there, that we were just not paying attention to the developments in Asia.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: I think we've come along in some ways in trying to rebalance but we have a long to go.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: And there's much at stake in how we deal with all the players in Asia.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: I'm hoping that the upcoming trip I have with President Xi Jinping produces some positive outcomes.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: I thought the climate agreement was quite consequential having been in Copenhagen in '09 with the President when we literally had to break into a meeting where the Chinese were consolidating India, South Africa and Brazil against any kind of movement toward the non advanced economies taking responsibility.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: So I think we've got some good stakes in the ground but we don't have a—a strategy yet that is going to be consistent.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: And the final thing I'll say about this, Martin, and I alluded to it in my remarks, I think one of our—one of our real problems right now is we don't have a consistent foreign policy that is bipartisan, let alone non-partisan.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: And I think that's a problem.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: I mean, I was appalled when those Republican senators wrote to the ayatollah.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: I thought it was incredibly, you know, short-sighted and you know, wrong-headed.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: And I don't think—I don't know what we rebuild a consistent foreign policy from administration to administration, regardless of Republican or Democrat.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: You know, it was a lot easier in a bipolar world, us versus the Soviet Union, I understand that, but I think we really have to work at it.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: And we can't work at it if we don't have a set of strategic pillars and organizing principles that we can present to our own people and present to the Congress and present to the world.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: So I think we have work to do.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: As to the first one, you know, it's always difficult in hindsight to say what could have happened if something different had been done.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: IF we remember back to that time, prime minister Cameron had lost the vote in the parliament.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: He wanted to show support for the president's policy of taking some limited military action in light of Syria's use of chemical weapons.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: So it became clear that there was going to be a difficult vote in the Congress, not clear at all that it would successful, which would have left the president with authority, certainly, with executive authority to act.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: But since it had become a public debate, it would have been a much more difficult decision for him to make.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: I do think that not being able to follow through on it cost us.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: I am certain of that.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: That still comes back in conversations that people have with me, both here at home and—and people from other countries, but I do think it was a net positive to get as much of the chemical weapons out as we could, and there was no way we could have done that without Russian cooperation.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: I think there was hope after that kind of cooperation produced positive results that then, we could go back to talking more broadly with the Russians about what needed to be done in Syria and what needed to be done with Assad.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: They did not reciprocate on that.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: So you know, I think it's like much in—in international relations, it's a—it's a mixed picture, some positive, you know, some—some negative.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: With respect to the refugees, I have said I think that you know, we're coming up on the U.N. General Assembly.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: I think there should be an emergency global gathering where the U.N. literally tries to get commitments.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: You know, we did that with Haiti.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: After the Haiti earthquake, we had a huge gathering at the U.N. where literally it was like a pledging conference, where we said, \"What are you going to do?\" What—you know, \"What can you contribute?\" And little countries to big countries all stepped up and it was a great show of support in the face of a terrible natural disaster.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: We need to do something similar, and I've—I've publicly called on the U.N. to convene such a gathering.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: I do it again today in front of all of you.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: The United States has to be at the table, has to be leading it.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: We were in a strong position to do that on Haiti.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: I think, even though it's not on our doorstep, we have a real interest in working not just with our European friends, I think this is a global responsibility.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: And if you're too far away or for whatever reason you don't think you can take refugees then you have to contribute money.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: You should be supporting not only those refugees fleeing, but the incredible work that Jordan and Lebanon and Turkey have been doing, and they have not gotten the financial support they need.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: In fact, the last I checked, the U.N. appeal had only reached 37 percent, so there is both financial work and contributions that need to be forthcoming and countries need to be more open and willing to take refugees.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: I obviously want the United States to do our part but I also want this to be a global response.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: So I hope that with all these leaders gathered, with Pope Francis addressing the United Nations General Assembly in just about two weeks, we can see something like that very visible with people literally making their commitments nation by nation, or in the case of the EU or other organizations as well.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: Well I'll restrain myself and answer the first questions first.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: I think there is an opportunity here to succeed, I really do.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: I don't think it's easy.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: But let's just go back a few years.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: Not so long ago, Israel and Turkey were working very closely together on a number of issues.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: Then came the flotilla and then came the response by the Israeli military, then came many years of you know, real hard feelings that got harder and harder and we lost what was a—not just a - a working relationship but a real bridge.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: Similarly, there have been a number of instances where in the past, Israel has worked in common concert with a number of the gulf countries.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: Israel is now back in a very productive relationship with Egypt, obviously with Jordan.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: So there are the pieces of national and regional interests here that I think very diligently and probably frustratingly could be pulled back together.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: I don't—I don't know that it's something the United States can lead, but it's certainly something that we can try to catalyze and encourage.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: And I think there is potential there because as I said in my speech, I will do everything I can to convince Turkey and (Qatar) that supporting Hamas is not in their interest.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: It's not in the region's interest.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: It's certainly not in Egypt's interest.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: They both care deeply about, you know, what happens in Egypt for somewhat different reasons than others, but they care.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: And so I think we have to build the case and I think American diplomats could help build that case.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: And then look for ways—I mean, I spent, you know, literally years trying to get the Israelis to finally apologize to the Turks on the flotilla.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: And there was a memorable day during one of my vacations where I was literally, you know, talking to the Israelis.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: I was talking to Henry Kissinger.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: I was talking to everybody I could find to make the strategic argument which we all believed, that the sooner Israel did that, the sooner they could get back to some kind of discussion perhaps.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: Finally that happened when President Obama went to Israel.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: And I was very happy that, you know, now we have a different Turkey with a different kind of, set of challenges, but interests remain the same.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: Turkey's interest for stability are not so different than they were, even though some of the leadership attitudes seem to have altered.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: So I would like to see us do everything we can.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: I would make a high priority of that.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: I hope that this administration in the last, you know, year-and-a-half or so of it, term, will be similarly doing that because, let's start seeing what we can do.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: It kind of goes back to Robin's question.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: You know, you don't know what you can achieve until you try to put the pieces together.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: And I think the more we can try to put those pieces together, the more we'll know whether or not something can come up.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: With respect to the lack of support for the agreement, honestly, I think it's—it's—it's in some instances genuine.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: Just as I said in my remarks, there are people who I deeply respect on the Democratic side certainly and I would respect them on the Republican side as well, who just have concerns that they don't feel have been answered.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: But I think the driving force behind it is, you know, to close ranks against the president, against this kind of diplomacy, but without offering an alternative.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: And that's what I find, I mean I don't mind debating alternatives.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: I mean, when we did the New Start Treaty, it was really hard to get the votes for that.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: I remember, you know, going up and making the case, but we got some Republican votes.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: But we're living in a very partisan atmosphere right now.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: And I do think we have to do more.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: Just as we, and I'll end with this by saying, just as we have to in diplomacy, reach out to people constantly, if not to persuade them to join with us, to eliminate an argument that they have, that they won't join, because they have been consulted.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC
texte: They have been brought along, they have been briefed.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: When they we're not turning on one another, the Republican hopefuls took turns turn—targeting Hillary Clinton in last night's debate.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: In a CNN exclusive, the Democratic presidential candidate, Hillary Clinton, joins us now live.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: This is her first live interview from the campaign trail.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: Madam Secretary, thanks very much for joining us.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: Great to talk to you, Wolf.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: I'm in Laconia, New Hampshire.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: You know, Wolf, I didn't get to see all of their debate, but I saw enough of it to know that this is just the usual back and forth political attacks, the kinds of things you say when you're on a debate stage and you really don't have much else to say.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: I didn't hear anything from any of them about how they're going to make college more affordable or get down student debt, or get equal pay for equal work for women, what they're going to do to make sure that we deal with the challenges of raising incomes for hardworking people.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: So I don't really pay a lot of attention to this kind of rhetoric that heats up the debate stage.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: They're all trying to vie for more attention from, obviously, the Republican Party.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: I'm going to let them decide how best to do it.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: But if anybody is interested, you know, there's a long list about what I have done and I'm very proud of it.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: You can read my book, \Hard Choices,\" read about how I negotiated a cease-fire between Israel and Hamas.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: You can read about how I put together the coalition that led to international sanctions against Iran.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: You can read about what I did when I was first lady to get the children's health insurance program, or as senator, working across the aisle on issues like getting better health care for our veterans.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: You know, this is just the silly season.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: I am looking forward to eventually debating on that stage whoever they finally nominate once they get around to doing that.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: You know, of course not... That's right.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: Well, Wolf, let's—let's break down what's happening here, because I think it's important.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: I know that there's a move on by some of the Republicans in the Congress to actually shut down the United States government over their demand that we no longer give federal funding to Planned Parenthood to perform the really necessary health services that they do for millions of women.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: So let's put aside for a moment here that there is no debate and there should be absolutely no argument that Planned Parenthood does cancer screenings, it helps provide family planning and contraceptive advice, it works to provide, you know, some of the most difficult kinds of counseling when it comes to giving an HIV test, for example.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: What this is about is the fact that some of the Planned Parenthood facilities perform abortions, which is legal under the laws of the United States.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: I understand that the Republican Party and particularly the candidates we heard from last night, wish that were not the case, wish that abortion were illegal and they could turn the clock back.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: So I think we ought to be very clear that Planned Parenthood has served to provide health care, necessary health care for millions of women.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: And I think it deserves not only our support, but the continuing funding from the federal government so that these women and girls who are seeking the kinds of services that are provided will be able to achieve that.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: Well, Wolf, let me tell you what I know, and that is there is a—a willingness on the part of Planned Parenthood to answer questions.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: They have been doing so.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: Some people may not want to hear the answers, but they have certainly put those answers out there into the public arena.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: And if the issue—the core issue that some on the stage last night or some in the Congress are trying to promote or trying to raise questions about has to do with the kind of research that is done legally in the United States, then that is an issue that goes far beyond any Planned Parenthood example.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: So I—I think it's important to sort out—there's a lot of emotion.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: There's a lot of accusations that are being hurled about.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: I think it's important to sort out and try to actually figure out what is going on.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: If it's the services that they are trying to shut down, like providing family planning or breast cancer screenings, that is just wrong and women deserve to be given support to get those services provided.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: If they want to shut down the legal provision of abortion services, then they've got a bigger problem, because, obviously, they—Planned Parenthood does not use federal dollars to do that.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: And if they are more focused on the research that is going on, then that's a set of issues that certainly is not only about Planned Parenthood.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: So I—I would hope... ?—that the Republicans, and particularly the Republicans in the House, led by Speaker Boehner, would not put our country and our economy in peril pursuing some kind of emotionally politically charged partisan attack on Planned Parenthood to shut our government down.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: I think that would be a very, very unfortunate decision.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: There's no evidence of that.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: And, again, this is—you know, this is overheated rhetoric, baseless charges trying to somehow, you know, gain a footing in the debate and in the primary.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: And it really doesn't deserve any comment.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: Well, you know, I was trying to explain, uh, what had happened and obviously it was clear that I should have used two different email accounts and I said that that was a mistake, I'm sorry, I've taken responsibility.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: But I've also, for more than a year now, been asking to testify before the Congressional committee that is investigating the situation in Benghazi, they would not let me appear.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: Finally—and I'm very happy about this—I will be appearing, toward the end of October, and I will look forward to answer all their questions.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: I'm trying to be as transparent as possible.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: That's why people are reading the contents of the emails that are being released.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: It's why I've turned over my server.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: It's why I will testify.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: Well, I—I've said for a long time, polls are going to go up, they're going to go down.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: I'm very confident and very comfortable about our strategy.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: I feel that our campaign in Iowa and New Hampshire, all the early states, and now we're moving on to the states that come after, are really coming together well.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: I'm excited by the level and intensity of the support that I have.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: So I always thought this would be a competitive election.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: I'm looking forward to it.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: This is an important job.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: This is the most important job not only in our country, but in the world.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: And people have to fight hard.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: They have to make their case and they have to earn the votes of the American voters.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: Well, Wolf, I'm not going to comment on a hypothetical and I'm certainly not going to comment on my good friend and former colleague.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: He has to make up his own mind about what's best for him and his family, as he wrestles with his choice.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: But I will tell the American people I believe that my set of experiences, my plans for the future, my vision for what America should be, what I've already told voters I would do on everything from making college affordable to paying down student debt to tackling climate change by making us the clean energy superpower, dealing with substance abuse and addiction, like I did here in New Hampshire today.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: I have a very comprehensive agenda that I think address the very issues that Americans are talking to me about.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: And I know that having been around the presidency, both as the first lady in the '90s and then as a member of President Obama's cabinet, working with other presidents, as a senator and even in private life, I feel very confident that I'm the right person at the right time to lead our country to deal with the growing issues around incomes that are not raising enough money for people to feel they've got a better future, about the kind of jobs we need more of, about how more workers get to share in the productivity by sharing the profits of what they helped produce.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: I'm the one out there talking very specifically about what I would do because I want to run a campaign that lays out my agenda, because when I get elected, I'm going to start working on it immediately.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: Well, Wolf, I have said from the very beginning, I look forward to debating.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: I look forward to the debate, you know, next month, you know, now just a month away.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: And I will certainly show up anywhere the Democratic National Committee tells us to show up, because I want us to have a good exchange of ideas and to make sure that Democratic voters first, and then general voters to follow, see exactly what we each stand for and what our positions are.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: So, you know, I—I am ready and willing, no matter what they decide to show up and be there.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: They can, you know, they made their decision.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: But I have made it clear that if they want to do more, I'm happy to do them.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: Oh, Wolf, you know, that—that's one of those questions that I cannot and will not answer.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: I think if you look at the last 35 years, actually, if you go back further, I think it's pretty indisputable that having a Democrat in the White House is good for our economy, better for our economy than the alternative.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: I think my husband understood that and produced.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: I think President Obama inherited a—a really big and dangerous mess and has, you know, been able to get us out of that ditch.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: So I'm not running for my husband's third term.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: I'm certainly not running for President Obama's third term.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: I'm running for my first term.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: But I do believe that both of them understood what it would take to try to clean up the messes they inherited from their Republican predecessors and begin to get the economy and the country working again for everybody.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: And that's exactly the kind of president I will be, as well.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: Thank you so much, Wolf.

titre: Interview with Wolf Blitzer of CNN
texte: Good to talk to you."

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: We're joined by Democratic presidential candidate and former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: Welcome, Secretary Clinton.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: We're glad to have you.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: Let's start in the news, Syrian refugees.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: Now, look, we're facing the worst refugee crisis since the end of World War II.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: And I think United States has to do more.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: And I would like to see us move from what is a good start with 10,000 to 65,000, and begin immediately to put into place the mechanisms for vetting the people that we would take in, looking to really emphasize some of those who are most vulnerable, a lot of the persecuted religious minorities, including Christians, and some who have been brutalized, like the Yazidi women.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: But I also want the United States to lead the world.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: And I have recommended that, at the upcoming U.N. General Assembly, there be an international meeting called by the secretary-general and literally get people to commit, putting money in, helping the front-line states, like Jordan and Turkey and Lebanon, who have absorbed a lot of refugees, working with the E.U.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: and the European countries, but getting everybody to make a contribution.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: Well, John, I did recommend that, at the beginning of this conflict, we do more to help train those who were in the forefront of leading the opposition against Assad, looking to try to bring the moderates together.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: A lot of these rebels, originally, they were—they were businesspeople, they were professional people, they were students.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: They had no training in going up against the Syrian army, which Assad clearly was going to use to the ultimate effect.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: That was not the decision taken at that time.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: A lot of what I worried about has happened.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: There are now big ungoverned territories within Syria that are dominated by terrorist groups, ISIS being the best known, but not the only one.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: You have Iran and Russia increasingly moving in to support Assad and his constant bombardment against his own people.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: And then you have these millions of refugees.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: So, where we are today is not where we were.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: And where we are today is that we have a failed program.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: You heard the testimony, five people trained for half—$500, half-a-billion dollars.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: But I think we still have to keep working with the Turks, with the Jordanians, with others of our partners.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: We also have to do more to support the Kurds, something that I have also advocated.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: Well, I hope we're not turning to the Russians.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: Let me just quickly say that I wouldn't give up on train and equip, but I sure would push the Pentagon to take hard look why what has been done has been such a failure and what more we could do to support, like, Kurdish fighters who are on the front lines.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: And one of the difficulties we had in the train and equip is that we basically were trying to train people to only take on ISIS and terrorist networks.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: We were not training and equipping them to take on Assad or his military or his proxies, which include Hezbollah, by the way.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: I hope we are not turning to the Russians in that way.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: I hope what we're doing—and this is what I support—and I heard Secretary Kerry say this is what we will be doing.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: And I think Secretary Carter has begun these conversations.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: First of all, we have to figure out what they are doing.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: Russia has a long interest in Syria.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: They have had a base in—a naval base in Syria for a long time.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: They have a connection because a lot of Syrians were educated in the Cold War in Moscow and a lot of Russians actually moved to Syria.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: So, they have not only deep links to Syria and Syrians, but they intend to support Assad for their own reasons.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: And we need to really unpeel what it is they're trying to accomplish and work with others to try to contain them.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: And I want to just end by saying, if they are providing any equipment to Hezbollah, if they are supporting Hezbollah, which is the main fighting force on behalf of the Iranians to support Assad, but also a deadly threat to Israel, then we have got to take action, whether there are tougher sanctions or other kinds of actions to try to prevent that from happening.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: I think it's a complicated question, because, of course, 9/11 happened.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: I was a senator from New York.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: And I was basically consumed by my responsibility to help the people directly affected in my state and in the city.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: And then I do give President Bush credit for trying to bring the country together around the threats that we did face.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: I have said the war in Iraq was a mistake.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: I supported what happened in Afghanistan.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: So, if you sort it all out, you know, it's a mixed—it's a mixed picture.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: I haven't seen that in a long time.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: I'm Hillary Clinton.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: And I approve this message.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: Well, of course it was a crisis.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: And we lost four brave Americans, including the person that I asked the president to send as ambassador, Chris Stevens.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: But we live in a dangerous world.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: And even our diplomats are at threat.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: And that goes all the way back to, for goodness' sake, taking over our embassy in Tehran or the bombings of our embassy in Beirut, when President Reagan was in charge.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: This is a dangerous world.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: And I think what we had to do during that period of time, in trying to protect our people after the attack on the consulate, getting them evacuated, not only working on what was going on in Libya, because, remember, we had embassies that were under attack or threatened to attack by terrorist groups across North Africa, indeed, across a much larger swathe of the world.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: So, I think it was terribly tragic, what happened.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: I immediately asked for an independent review, just like former secretaries of state did.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: And I made that public.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: And the only other person who did that was Secretary Albright after our embassies were bombed in Africa.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: So, my view on this is, we have to learn things.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: And we are always learning.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: We learned after Beirut.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: We learned after Tanzania and Kenya.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: We have learned after Benghazi, but we're not going to be able to represent the United States working out of hermetically sealed tanks.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: We are going to have to be out in the world.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: Well, I just don't think that's fair.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: And I'm going to testify about this at the end of October before the committee looking into this.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: I think it's the eighth investigation that the Congress has conducted.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: There were two things going on simultaneously.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: I and others said that we were attacked.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: There was no doubt about that.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: That video, which was still spinning through the world, was being mentioned on social media.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: We had people climbing the walls at our embassy in Cairo even before the attack in Benghazi.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: And we had a lot of other attacks.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: I had to call the president of one of our neighboring countries, Tunis, to try to get—in Tunis—to get them to help protect our embassy.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: So, I was worried about everything that was going on and how people were responding to that from North Africa to Pakistan, all the way to Indonesia.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: Well, all I can tell you, I never felt any political pressure or did I feel any political reason to do anything other than what we tried to do, which was to immediately deal with the problems that were coming at us.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: Well, look, I have said that I didn't make the best choice.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: I should have used two separate e-mail accounts, one personal, one work-related.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: What I did was allowed.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: It was fully above board.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: People in the government certainly knew that I was using a personal e-mail.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: But I have tried to be transparent.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: And that includes releasing 55,000 pages, which is unprecedented—nobody else that I'm aware of has ever done that—plus turning over the server, plus testifying at the end of October.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: So, I think that people have questions.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: I want to try to answer them.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: Well, look, it was permitted.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: And I think that people can make their own judgments about that.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: But I have tried to be as transparent as I can.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: Well, it wasn't that long.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: What I did was to send e-mails to people at their government accounts, which I had every reason to believe would be captured on the government systems.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: And when we were asked to help the State Department make sure they had everything from other secretaries of state, not just me, I'm the one who said, OK, great, I will go through them again.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: And we provided all of them.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: And more than 90 percent were already in the system.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: And, in fact, I gave so many that were not work-related, just to be as comprehensive as possible, they are already sending back about 1,200 of them.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: So, look, I did what was, as I said, allowed.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: I said it wasn't the best choice.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: And it turned out to be a mistake, in retrospect.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: But, at the time, and given the fact that most of them were in the government systems, people are going to get a chance to see all kinds of behind-the-scenes conversations, most of which, I'm embarrassed to say, are kind of boring.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: Well, you know, I'm sorry that I made a choice that has raised all of these questions, because I don't like reading that people have questions about what I did and how I did it.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: But so far as I am aware, what they did, despite the way it was portrayed, is within the laws that were set up for this.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: This is one of those really painful questions that people raise.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: And, obviously, it's really emotional.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""
texte: And I have been in the public eye for so long that I think—you know, it's like the feature that you see in some magazines sometimes.

titre: Interview with John Dickerson of CBS News \Face the Nation\""

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""

texte: Thank you very much.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: That's true—absolutely.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: I want to have a much more transparent government and I think we now have the tools to make that happen.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: I want to have as much information about the way our government operates on the Internet.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: So the people who pay for it, the taxpayers of America, can see that.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: Well, Chuck, let me make a couple points.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: First of all, as I have said very often, all of the e-mails that I sent were intended to be in the government systems if they were work related.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: That's why I sent them to people at their work a dresses.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: And, you know, the vast majority of them ended up there.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: So I have said also that if I had to do it all over again I would have used a separate e-mail account.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: I did it for convenience and it turned out not to be that at all.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: But the bottom line is my e-mails were predominantly in the State Department system or on other government servers and then I said I'm going to give them all after a very careful review and I did so.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: Well, everything that we had access to was certainly out there and the reason we know about the e-mail chain with General Petraeus is because it was on a government server.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: And so from my perspective we have a very thorough review process that we conducted and my attorneys supervised it, they went through everything and what we had available at the time was turned over.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: There was a transition period.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: I wasn't that focused on my e-mail account to be clear here.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: Yes, but it was already there.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: It had been there for years.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: It is the system that my husband's personal office used when he got out of the White House so it was sitting there in the basement.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: It was not any trouble at all.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: I know there are a lot of people who are questioning that.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: But the fact is that it was there.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: I added my account to it.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: And I think it's also fair to say that there are some things about this that I just can't control.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: I can't control the technical aspects of it.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: I relied on people who were and we have done everything we could in response to the State Department asking us to do this review because they asked all the former secretaries.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: And the reason they asked, Chuck, is because they found gaps in their own recordkeeping.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: I think I have done all that I can to take responsibility to be as transparent as possibly in turning over 55,000 pages, in turning over my server and to testify on October 22, which I've been asking to do before the Congress.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: Well, we have explained that.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: The campaign has explained it.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: Look, when the committee—the eighth or ninth committee—investigating Benghazi asked for information from the State Department, they were doing a survey and they found discrepancies in their recordkeeping not in my records per se but in their overall recordkeeping.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: There were gaps and that's why they sent the letter and that's why we did the overall comprehensive search for everything.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: And it got us to the same place—we looked through everything, we gave them everything work-related.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: That never crossed my mind.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: That's how the Benghazi Committee got the e-mails even before we went through our exhaustive process.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: That was the outcome.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: And it is regrettable but it's part of the system.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: Well, it is like a drip-drip-drip and that's why I said there's only so much that I can control.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: But what I have tried to do in explaining this is to provide more transparency and more information than anybody that I'm aware of has ever served in the government and I'm happy to do that because I want these questions to be answered.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: I can't predict to you what the Republicans will come up with, what kind of charges or claims they might make.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: I have no control over that.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: I can only do the best I can to try to respond.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: The Justice Department has the e-mails, they have the server.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: They're conducting a security inquiry.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: They will take whatever necessary steps are required to get this matter resolved.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: All I can tell you is that when my attorneys conducted this exhaustive process I did not participate.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: I didn't look at them.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: I wanted them to be as clear in their process as possible.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: I didn't want to be looking over their shoulder.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: If not then it would not.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: As I just said, over 1,200 of the e-mails that we were overly inclusive in trying to be comprehensive the State Department has said we don't want these.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: These aren't work related.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: They're sending them back.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: So when that process finished, you know, my attorney said what do you want us to do with all these personal e-mails?

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: I said I don't need to keep them.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: I don't need them or want them.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: So they then talked to the IT server, the technical people who were responsible for maintaining them and said we don't need them anymore.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: That's the limit of my knowledge and I know I was a little sarcastic in one exchange with the press for which I—I'm sorry guys.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: But you know, I'm not a technical expert.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: I just said I don't need them.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: That was handled by, you know, the professionals and others in the State Department.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: Well, you know, let me say this Chuck.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: I have tried to the best of my ability to be able to respond and if people are uncertain, if they have concerns about these questions around the e-mails it's their choice to say that's going to influence, you know, how I think about the election.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: I understand that, I get it.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: But I also hope people will look at my life long advocacy for kids and families and women and look at what I'm proposing, the vision I have for the country to move forward on everything from raising incomes to equal pay for equal work to getting the cost of college down to dealing with high prescription drug costs—that's what I hope people focus on and people get to make their minds up.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: That's the beauty of our process.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: People can decide on whatever basis they choose.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: Well, first of all, I love my husband and he does get upset when I am attacked.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: But we also get the fact that, look, this is a contest and it's fair game for people to raise whatever they choose to raise.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: As he said I think in that same interview, they're not giving this job away, you have to get out there, you have to earn it.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""

texte: And of course I take responsibility.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: It was a mistake back when I did it and I'm trying to do the best I can to answer all of the questions that people have.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: And as I said during the 90s I was subjected to the same kind of barrage and it was—it seemed to be at the time endless.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: And I trust the voters to make that decision this time around, too.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""
texte: So it is with conviction that I support this resolution as being in the best interest of our nation.

titre: Interview with Chuck Todd of NBC's \Meet the Press\""

titre: Interview with Al Sharpton of MSNBC's \Politics Nation\""

titre: Interview with Al Sharpton of MSNBC's \Politics Nation\""

titre: Interview with Al Sharpton of MSNBC's \Politics Nation\""

titre: Interview with Al Sharpton of MSNBC's \Politics Nation\""

titre: Interview with Al Sharpton of MSNBC's \Politics Nation\""

titre: Interview with Al Sharpton of MSNBC's \Politics Nation\""

titre: Interview with Al Sharpton of MSNBC's \Politics Nation\""

titre: Interview with Al Sharpton of MSNBC's \Politics Nation\""

titre: Interview with Al Sharpton of MSNBC's \Politics Nation\""

titre: Interview with Al Sharpton of MSNBC's \Politics Nation\""

titre: Interview with Al Sharpton of MSNBC's \Politics Nation\""
texte: I like an infrastructure bank that will put more people to work.

titre: Interview with Al Sharpton of MSNBC's \Politics Nation\""

titre: Interview with Al Sharpton of MSNBC's \Politics Nation\""
texte: And the worst thing that could happen to our country, in my opinion, is for the Republicans to rip away that progress and to do a big U-turn back to trickle-down economics to slam the door in the face of hard working people, whether it's working women or minorities of any sort or the LGBT community, to basically begin to marginalize and you know, dismiss the contributions of so many of our fellow Americans.

titre: Interview with Al Sharpton of MSNBC's \Politics Nation\""

titre: Interview with Al Sharpton of MSNBC's \Politics Nation\""
