titre: Interview with Al Sharpton of MSNBC's \Politics Nation\""
texte: A lot of people are very appreciative of the work I did as secretary of state.

titre: Interview with Al Sharpton of MSNBC's \Politics Nation\""

titre: Interview with Al Sharpton of MSNBC's \Politics Nation\""
texte: So I think the number of people both in my campaign and on the ground, around the country who are supporting me who were first and foremost supporters of President Obama speaks very well to their understanding of how hard this job is and how they need to elect somebody, a Democrat, who can build on the successes of the Obama presidency, and that's what I am pledged to do.

titre: Interview with Al Sharpton of MSNBC's \Politics Nation\""
texte: You know, everywhere I go to speak around the country, I talk about the mess that President Obama inherited from his Republican predecessors, not unlike although much worse than what my husband inherited from his Republican predecessors.

titre: Interview with Al Sharpton of MSNBC's \Politics Nation\""
texte: And what I say is I'm not running for President Obama's third term or for Bill Clinton's third term.

titre: Interview with Al Sharpton of MSNBC's \Politics Nation\""
texte: I'm running for my first term.

titre: Interview with Al Sharpton of MSNBC's \Politics Nation\""
texte: But I know what works and I know how important it is to stand up for our values, to stand up for our interests and our security in a way that makes sense which is smart.

titre: Interview with Al Sharpton of MSNBC's \Politics Nation\""
texte: So people who have supported President Obama are, you know, very enthusiastic and I'm grateful for that in support of my candidacy.

titre: Interview with Al Sharpton of MSNBC's \Politics Nation\""

titre: Interview with Al Sharpton of MSNBC's \Politics Nation\""

titre: Interview with Al Sharpton of MSNBC's \Politics Nation\""
texte: And we have different ways of going about it, about how we want to make college affordable, how we're going to deal with the affordable care act.

titre: Interview with Al Sharpton of MSNBC's \Politics Nation\""

titre: Interview with Al Sharpton of MSNBC's \Politics Nation\""

titre: Interview with Al Sharpton of MSNBC's \Politics Nation\""

titre: Interview with Al Sharpton of MSNBC's \Politics Nation\""

titre: Interview with Al Sharpton of MSNBC's \Politics Nation\""

titre: Interview with Al Sharpton of MSNBC's \Politics Nation\""
texte: But I think at the end of the day when I put forth, you know, my views about what the country should be doing and it is in conjunction with my experience and I think my ability, my determination, my tenacity to get things done, people will respond to that, caucus for me and vote for me.

titre: Interview with Al Sharpton of MSNBC's \Politics Nation\""

titre: Interview with Al Sharpton of MSNBC's \Politics Nation\""

titre: Interview with Al Sharpton of MSNBC's \Politics Nation\""
texte: You know, I find that so insulting, so demeaning and condescending, it's the kind of language we've heard not only from Jeb Bush, we heard it from Mitt Romney.

titre: Interview with Al Sharpton of MSNBC's \Politics Nation\""

titre: Interview with Al Sharpton of MSNBC's \Politics Nation\""

titre: Interview with Al Sharpton of MSNBC's \Politics Nation\""

titre: Interview with Al Sharpton of MSNBC's \Politics Nation\""

titre: Interview with Jake tapper of CNN's \State of the Union\""

titre: Interview with Jake tapper of CNN's \State of the Union\""

titre: Interview with Jake tapper of CNN's \State of the Union\""

titre: Interview with Jake tapper of CNN's \State of the Union\""

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: Thank you Mr. Chairman, Ranking Member Cummings, members of the committee.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: The terrorist attacks at our diplomatic compound and later, at the CIA post in Benghazi, Libya on September 11, 2012 took the lives of four brave Americans: Ambassador Chris Stevens, Sean Smith, Glen Doherty, and Tyrone Woods.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: I am here to honor the service of those four men, the courage of the Diplomatic Security agency and the CIA officers who risked their lives that night, and the work their colleagues do every single day all over the world.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: I knew and admired Chris Stevens.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: He was one of our nation's most accomplished diplomats.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: Chris's mother liked to say that he had sand in his shoes, because he was always moving, always working, especially in the Middle East that he came to know so well.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: When the revolution broke out in Libya, we named Chris as our envoy to the opposition.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: There was no easy way to get him into Benghazi to begin gathering information and meeting those Libyans who were rising up against the murderous the dictator Qadhafi, but he found a way to get himself there on a Greek cargo ship, just like a 19th century American envoy.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: But his work was very much 21st century hard-nosed diplomacy.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: It is a testament to the relationships that he built in Libya that on the day following the awareness of his death, tens of thousands of Libyans poured into the streets in Benghazi.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: They held signs reading \thugs don't represent Benghazi or Islam.\" \"Sorry people of America, this is not the behavior of our Islam or our Prophet.\" \"Chris Stevens, a friend to all Libyans.\" Although I didn't have the privilege of meeting Sean Smith personally, he was a valued member of our State Department family.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: An Air Force veteran, he was an Information Management officer, who had served in Pretoria, Baghdad, Montreal, and The Hague.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: Tyrone Woods and Glen Doherty worked for the CIA.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: They were killed by mortar fire at the CIA's outpost in Benghazi, a short distance from the diplomatic compound.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: They were both former Navy SEALs and trained paramedics with distinguished records of service, including in Iraq and Afghanistan.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: As Secretary of State, I had the honor to lead and the responsibility to support nearly 70,000 diplomats and development experts across the globe.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: Losing any one of them, as we did in Iraq, Afghanistan, Mexico, Haiti, and Libya during my tenure, was deeply painful for our entire State Department and USAID family, and for me personally.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: I was the one who asked Chris to go to Libya as our envoy.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: I was the one who recommended him to be our Ambassador to to the President.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: After the attacks, I stood next to President Obama as Marines carried his casket and those of the other three Americans off the plane at Andrews Air Force Base.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: I took responsibility.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: And, as part of that, before I left office, I launched reforms to better protect our people in the field and help reduce the chance of another tragedy happening in the future.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: What happened in Benghazi has been scrutinized by a nonpartisan, hard-hitting Accountability Review Board, seven prior Congressional investigations, multiple news organizations, and, of course, our law enforcement and intelligence agencies.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: So today I would like to share three observations about how we can learn from this tragedy and move forward as a nation.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: First, America must lead in a dangerous world, and our diplomats must continue representing us in dangerous places.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: The State Department sends people to more than 270 posts in 170 countries around the world.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: Chris Stevens understood that diplomats must operate in many places where our soldiers do not, where there are no other boots on the ground, and safety is far from guaranteed.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: In fact, he volunteered for just those assignments.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: He also understood we will never prevent every act of terrorism or achieve perfect security, and that we inevitably must accept a level of risk to protect our country and advance our interests and values.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: And make no mistake: the risks are real.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: Terrorists have killed more than sixty-five American diplomatic personnel since the 1970s and more than a hundred contractors and locally employed staff.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: Since 2001, there have been more than one hundred attacks on U.S. diplomatic facilities around the world.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: But if you ask our most experienced ambassadors, they'll tell you they can't do their jobs for us from bunkers.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: It would compound the tragedy of Benghazi if Chris Stevens' death and the death of the other three Americans ended up undermining the work to which he and they devoted their lives.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: We have learned the hard way when America is absent, especially from unstable places, there are consequences.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: Extremism takes root, aggressors seek to fill the vacuum, and security everywhere is threatened, including here at home.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: That's why Chris was in Benghazi.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: It's why he had served previously in Syria, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, and Jerusalem during the second intifada.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: Nobody knew the dangers of Libya better – a weak government, extremist groups, rampant instability.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: But Chris chose to go to Benghazi because he understood America had to be represented there at that pivotal time.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: He knew that eastern Libya was where the revolution had begun and that unrest there could derail the country's fragile transition to democracy.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: And if extremists gained a foothold, they would have the chance to destabilize the entire region, including Egypt and Tunisia.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: He also knew how urgent it was to ensure that the weapons Qadhafi had left strewn across the country, including shoulder-fired missiles that could knock an airplane out of the sky, did not fall into the wrong hands.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: The nearest Israeli airport is just a day's drive from the Libyan border.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: Above all, Chris understood that most people, in Libya or anywhere, reject the extremists' argument that violence can ever be a path to dignity or justice.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: That's what those thousands of Libyans were saying after they learned of his death.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: He understood there was no substitute for going beyond the Embassy walls and doing the hard work of building relationships.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: Retreat from the world is not an option.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: America cannot shrink from our responsibility to lead.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: That doesn't mean we should ever return to the go-it-alone foreign policy of the past, a foreign policy that puts boots on the ground as a first choice rather than a last resort.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: We need creative, confident leadership that harnesses all of America's strengths and values.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: Leadership that integrates and balances the tools of diplomacy, development, and defense.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: And at the heart of that effort must be dedicated professionals like Chris Stevens and his colleagues, who put their lives on the line for a country—our country—because they believed – as I do – that America is the greatest force for peace and progress the world has ever known.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: My second observation is this: We have a responsibility to provide our diplomats with the resources and support they need to do their jobs as safely and effectively as possible.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: After previous deadly attacks, leaders from both parties and both branches of government came together to determine what went wrong and how to fix it for the future.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: That's what happened during the Reagan administration, when Hezbollah attacked our embassy.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: They killed 63 people, including 17 Americans.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: And then in a later attack, attacked our Marine barracks and killed so many more.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: Those two attacks in Beirut resulted in the deaths of 258 Americans.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: It's what happened during the Clinton administration when al Qaeda bombed our embassies in Kenya and Tanzania, killing more than two hundred people, wounding more than two thousand people, and killing twelve Americans.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: It's what happened during the Bush administration after 9/11.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: Part of America's strength is we learn, we adapt, and we get stronger.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: After the Benghazi attacks, I asked Ambassador Thomas Pickering, one of our most distinguished and longest-serving diplomats, along with Admiral Mike Mullen, the former Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff appointed by President George W. Bush, to lead an Accountability Review Board.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: This is an institution that the Congress set up after the terrible attacks in Beirut.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: There have been eighteen previous Accountability Review Boards.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: Only two have ever made any of their findings public.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: The one following the attacks on our embassies in East Africa and the one following the attack on Benghazi.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: The Accountability Review Board did not pull a single punch.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: They found systemic problems and management deficiencies in two State Department bureaus.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: And the Review Board recommended twenty-nine specific improvements.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: I pledged that by the time I left office, every one would be on the way to implementation.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: More Marines were slated for deployment to high-threat embassies.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: Additional Diplomatic Security agents were being hired and trained.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: And Secretary Kerry has continued this work.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: But there is more to do.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: And no administration can do it alone.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: Congress has to be our partner, as it has been after previous tragedies.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: For example, the Accountability Review Board and subsequent investigations have recommended improved training for our officers before they deploy to the field.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: But efforts to establish a modern joint training center are being held up by Congress.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: The men and women who serve our country deserve better.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: Finally, there is one more observation I'd like to share: I traveled to 112 countries as Secretary of State.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: Every time I did, I felt great pride and honor representing the country that I love.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: We need leadership at home to match our leadership abroad.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: Leadership that puts national security ahead of politics and ideology.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: Our nation has a long history of bipartisan cooperation on foreign policy and national security.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: Not that we always agree — far from it — but we do come together when it counts.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: As Secretary of State, I worked with the Republican chairman of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee to pass a landmark nuclear arms control treaty with Russia.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: I worked with Republican Leader, Senator Mitch McConnell, to open up Burma, now Myanmar, to find democratic change.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: I know it's possible to find common ground, because I have done it.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: We should debate on the basis of fact, not fear.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: We should resist denigrating the patriotism or loyalty of those with who we disagree.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: Despite all the previous investigations and all the talk about partisan agendas, I am here to honor those we lost and to do what I can to aid those who serve us still.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: And my challenge to you, members of this Committee, is the same challenge I put to myself.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: Let's be worthy of the trust the American people have bestowed upon us.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: They expect us to lead.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: To learn the right lessons.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: To rise above partisanship and to reach for statesmanship.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: That's what I tried to do every day as Secretary of State.

titre: Opening Statement to House Select Committee on Benghazi
texte: And it's what I hope we all strive for here today and into the future.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: Thank you very much.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: [ ] Thank you, Richard.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: And thanks for the great work that the council does under your leadership.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: It truly is an important resource for us all.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: Fareed, I look forward to having the conversation with you, everyone here at the council, and Mr. Mayor.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: Thank you very much for being here and for everything you are doing and will do to keep our city safe and strong.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: I wanted to come here to our city, which has shown such resilience in the face of terrorism, to talk about the events of the past week, and the work we must do together to protect our country and our friends.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: When the United States was hit on 9/11, our allies treated that attack against one as an attack against all.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: Now, it's our turn to stand in solidarity with France and all of our friends.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: We cherish the same values.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: We face the same adversaries.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: We must share the same determination.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: After a major terrorist attack, every society faces a choice between fear and resolve.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: The world's great democracies can't sacrifice our values or turn our backs on those in need.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: Therefore, we must choose resolve.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: And we must lead the world to meet this threat.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: Now, let's be clear about what we're facing.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: Beyond Paris in recent days, we've seen deadly terrorist attacks in Nigeria, Lebanon, Iraq and Turkey, and a Russian civilian airline destroyed over the Sinai.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: At the heart of today's new landscape of terror is ISIS.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: They persecute religious and ethnic minorities; kidnap and behead civilians; murder children.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: They systematically enslave, torture and rape women and girls.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: ISIS operates across three mutually reinforcing dimensions: a physical enclave in Iraq and Syria; an international terrorist network that includes affiliates across the region and beyond; and an ideological movement of radical jihadism.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: We have to target and defeat all three, and time is of the essence.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: ISIS is demonstrating new ambition, reach and capabilities.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: We have to break the group's momentum and then its back.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: Our goal is not to deter or contain ISIS, but to defeat and destroy ISIS.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: But we have learned that we can score victories over terrorist leaders and networks, only to face metastasizing threats down the road, so we also have to play and win the long game.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: We should pursue a comprehensive counterterrorism strategy, one that embeds our mission against ISIS within a broader struggle against radical jihadism that is bigger than any one group, whether it's Al Qaida or ISIS or some other network.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: An immediate war against an urgent enemy and a generational struggle against an ideology with deep roots will not be easily torn out.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: It will require sustained commitment in every pillar of American power.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: This is a worldwide fight, and American must lead it.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: Our strategy should have three main elements.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: One, defeat ISIS in Syria, Iraq and across the Middle East; two, disrupt and dismantle the growing terrorist infrastructure that facilitates the flow of fighters, financing arms and propaganda around the world; three, harden our defenses and those of our allies against external and homegrown threats.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: Let me start with the campaign to defeat ISIS across the region.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: The United States and our international coalition has been conducting this fight for more than a year.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: It's time to begin a new phase and intensify and broaden our efforts to smash the would-be caliphate and deny ISIS control of territory in Iraq and Syria.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: That starts with a more effective coalition air campaign, with more allied planes, more strikes and a broader target set.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: A key obstacle standing in the way is a shortage of good intelligence about ISIS and its operations, so we need an immediate intelligence surge in the region, including technical assets, Arabic speakers with deep expertise in the Middle East and even closer partnership with regional intelligence services.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: Our goal should be to achieve the kind of penetration we accomplished with Al Qaida in the past.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: This would help us identify and eliminate ISIS' command and control and its economic lifelines.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: A more effective coalition air campaign is necessary, but not sufficient, and we should be honest about the fact that to be successful, airstrikes will have to be combined with ground forces actually taking back more territory from ISIS.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: Like President Obama, I do not believe that we should again have 100,000 American troops in combat in the Middle East.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: If we have learned anything from 15 years of war in Iraq and Afghanistan, it's that local people and nations have to secure their own communities.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: We can help them, and we should, but we cannot substitute for them.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: Now, the obstacles to achieving this are significant.

texte: On the Iraqi side of the border, Kurdish forces have fought bravely to defend their own lands and to re-take towns from ISIS, but the Iraqi national army has struggled, and it's going to take more work to get it up to fighting shape.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: As part of that process, we may have to give our own troops advising and training the Iraqis greater freedom of movement and flexibility, including embedding in local units and helping target airstrikes.

texte: Ultimately, however, a ground campaign in Iraq will only succeed if more Iraqi Sunnis join the fight.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City

texte: In the first Sunni awakening in 2007, we were able to provide sufficient support and assurances to the Sunni tribes to persuade them to join us in rooting out Al Qaida.

texte: Unfortunately, under Prime Minister Maliki's rule, those tribes were betrayed and forgotten.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: But nonetheless, we need to lay the foundation for a second Sunni awakening.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: We need to put sustained pressure on the government in Baghdad to get its political house in order, move forward with national reconciliation, and finally stand up a national guard.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: Baghdad needs to accept, even embrace, arming Sunni and Kurdish forces in the war against ISIS.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: But if Baghdad won't do that, the coalition should do so directly.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: On the Syrian side, the big obstacle to getting more ground forces to engage ISIS, beyond the Syrian Kurds who are already deep in the fight, is that the viable Sunni opposition groups remain understandably preoccupied with fighting Assad who, let us remember, has killed many more Syrians than the terrorists have.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: But they are increasingly under threat from ISIS as well.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: So we need to move simultaneously toward a political solution to the civil war that paves the way for a new government with new leadership, and to encourage more Syrians to take on ISIS as well.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: To support them, we should immediately deploy the special operations force President Obama has already authorized, and be prepared to deploy more as more Syrians get into the fight.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: And we should retool and ramp up our efforts to support and equip viable Syrian opposition units.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: Our increased support should go hand in hand with increased support from our Arab and European partners, including special forces who can contribute to the fight on the ground.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: We should also work with the coalition and the neighbors to impose no-fly zones that will stop Assad from slaughtering civilians and the opposition from the air.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: Opposition forces on the ground, with material support from the coalition, could then help create safe areas where Syrians could remain in the country, rather than fleeing toward Europe.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: This combined approach would help enable the opposition to retake the remaining stretch of the Turkish border from ISIS, choking off its supply lines.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: It would also give us new leverage in the diplomatic process that Secretary Kerry is pursuing.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: Of course, we've been down plenty of diplomatic dead-ends before in this conflict.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: But we have models for how seemingly intractable multi-sectarian civil wars do eventually end.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: We can learn lessons from Lebanon and Bosnia about what it will take.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: And Russia and Iran have to face the fact that continuing to prop up a vicious dictator will not bring stability.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: Right now, I'm afraid, President Putin is actually making things somewhat worse.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: Now, to be clear, though, there is an important role for Russia to help in resolving the conflict in Syria.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: And we have indicated a willingness to work with them toward an outcome that preserves Syria as a unitary, nonsectarian state, with protections for the rights of all Syrians and to keep key state institutions intact.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: There is no alternative to a political transition that allows Syrians to end Assad's rule.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: Now, much of this strategy on both sides of the border hinges on the roles of our Arab and Turkish partners.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: And we must get them to carry their share of the burden, with military intelligence and financial contributions, as well as using their influence with fighters and tribes in Iraq and Syria.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: Countries like Jordan have offered more, and we should take them up on it, because ultimately our efforts will only succeed if the Arabs and Turks step up in a much bigger way.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: This is their fight and they need to act like it.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: So far, however, Turkey has been more focused on the Kurds than on countering ISIS.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: And to be fair, Turkey has a long and painful history with Kurdish terrorist groups.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: But the threat from ISIS cannot wait.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: As difficult as it may be, we need to get Turkey to stop bombing Kurdish fighters in Syria who are battling ISIS, and become a full partner in our coalition efforts against ISIS.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: The United States should also work with our Arab partners to get them more invested in the fight against ISIS.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: At the moment, they're focused in other areas because of their concerns in the region, especially the threat from Iran.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: That's why the Saudis, for example, shifted attention from Syria to Yemen.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: So we have to work out a common approach.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: In September, I laid out a comprehensive plan to counter Iranian influence across the region and its support for terrorist proxies such as Hezbollah and Hamas.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: We cannot view Iran and ISIS as separate challenges.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: Regional politics are too interwoven.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: Raising the confidence of our Arab partners and raising the costs to Iran for bad behavior will contribute to a more effective fight against ISIS.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: And as we work out a broader regional approach, we should, of course, be closely consulting with Israel, our strongest ally in the Middle East.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: Israel increasingly shares with our Arab partners and has the opportunity to do more in intelligence and joint efforts as well.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: Now, we should have no illusions about how difficult the mission before us really is.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: We have to fit a lot of pieces together, bring along a lot of partners, move on multiple fronts at once.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: But if we press forward on both sides of the border, in the air and on the ground, as well as diplomatically, I do believe we can crush ISIS's enclave of terror.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: And to support this campaign, Congress should swiftly pass an updated authorization to use military force.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: That will send a message to friend and foe alike that the United States is committed to this fight.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: The time for delay is over.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: We should get this done.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: Now, the second element of our strategy looks beyond the immediate battlefield of Iraq and Syria, to disrupt and dismantle global terrorist infrastructure on the ground and online.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: A terror pipeline that facilitates the flow of fighters, financing, arms and propaganda around the world has allowed ISIS to strike at the heart of Paris last week and an Al Qaida affiliate to do the same at Charlie Hebdo earlier this year.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: ISIS is working hard to extend its reach, establish affiliates and cells far from its home base, and despite the significant setbacks it has encountered, not just with ISIS and its ambitious plans, but even Al Qaida, including the death of Osama bin Laden, they are still posing great threats to so many.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: Let's take one example.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: We've had a lot of conversation about ISIS in the last week, let's not forget Al Qaida.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: They still have the most sophisticated bombmakers, ambitious plotters and active affiliates in places like Yemen and North Africa, so we can't just focus on Iraq and Syria, we need to intensify our counter—our counterterrorism efforts on a wider scope.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: Most urgent is stopping the flow of foreign fighters to and from the war zones of the Middle East.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: Thousands—thousands of young recruits have flocked to Syria from France, Germany, Belgium, the United Kingdom and, yes, even the United States.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: Their western passports make it easier for them to cross borders and eventually return home radicalized and battle hardened.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: Stemming this tide will require much better coordination and information-sharing among countries every step of the way.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: We should not stop pressing until Turkey, where most foreign fighters cross into Syria, finally locks down its border.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: The United States and our allies need to know and share the identities of every fighter who has traveled to Syria.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: We also have to be smart and target interventions that will have the greatest impact.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: For example, we need a greater focus on shutting down key enablers who arrange transportation, documents and more.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: When it comes to terrorist financing, we have to go after the nodes that facilitate illicit trade and transactions.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: The U.N. Security Council should update its terrorism sanctions.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: They have a resolution that does try to block terrorist financing and other enabling activities, but we have to place more obligations on countries to police their own banks, and the United States, which has quite a record of success in this area, can share more intelligence to help other countries.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: And once and for all, the Saudis, the Qataris and others need to stop their citizens from directly funding extremist organizations as well as the schools and mosques around the world that have set too many young people on a path to radicalization.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: When it comes to blocking terrorist recruitment, we have to identify the hotspots, the specific neighborhoods and villages, the prisons and schools where recruitment happens in clusters, like the neighborhood in Brussels where the Paris attacks were planned.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: Through partnerships with local law enforcement and civil society, especially with Muslim community leaders, we have to work to tip the balance away from extremism in these hotspots.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: Radicalization and recruitment also is happening online.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: There's no doubt we have to do a better job contesting online space, including websites and chat rooms where jihadists communicate with followers.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: We must deny them virtual territory just as we deny them actual territory.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: At the State Department, I built up a unit of communication specialists fluent in Urdu, Arabic, Somali and other languages to battle with extremists online.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: We need more of that, including from the private sector.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: Social media companies can also do their part by swiftly shutting down terrorist accounts, so they're not used to plan, provoke or celebrate violence.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: Online or off-line, the bottom line is that we are in a contest of ideas against an ideology of hate, and we have to win.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: Let's be clear, though, Islam is not our adversary.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: Muslims are peaceful and tolerant people, and have nothing whatsoever to do with terrorism.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: The obsession in some quarters with a clash of civilization, or repeating the specific words radical Islamic terrorism isn't just a distraction, it gives these criminals, these murderers more standing than they deserve.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: It actually plays into their hands by alienating partners we need by our side.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: Our priority should be how to fight the enemy.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: In the end, it didn't matter what kind of terrorist we call bin Laden, it mattered that we killed bin Laden.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: But we still can't close our eyes to the fact that there is a distorted and dangerous stream of extremism within the Muslim world that continues to spread.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: Its adherents are relatively few in number, but capable of causing profound damage, most especially to their own communities throughout an arc of instability that stretches from North and West Africa to Asia.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: Overlapping conflicts, collapsing state structures, widespread corruption, poverty and repression have created openings for extremists to exploit.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: Before the Arab Spring, I warned that the region's foundations would sink into the sand without immediate reforms.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: Well, the need has only grown more urgent.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: We have to join with our partners to do the patient's steady work of empowering moderates and marginalizing extremists; supporting democratic institutions and the rule of law; creating economic growth that supports stability; working to curb corruption, helping training effective and accountable law enforcement, intelligence and counterterrorism services.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: As we do this, we must be building up a global counterterrorism infrastructure that is more active and adaptable than the terror networks we're trying to defeat.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: When I became secretary of State, I was surprised to find that nearly a decade after 9/11, there was still no dedicated international vehicle to regularly convene key countries to deal with terrorist threats.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: So, we created the Global Counterterrorism Forum, which now brings together nearly 30 countries, many from the Muslim world.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: It should be a clearing house for directing assistance to countries that need it, for mobilizing common action against threats.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: And let's not lose sight of the global cooperation needed to lock down loose nuclear material and chemical and biological weapons, and keep them out of the hands of terrorists.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: At the end of the day, we still must be prepared to go after terrorists wherever they plot using all the tools at our disposal, that includes targeted strikes by U.S. military aircraft and drones, with proper safeguards when there are any other viable options to deal with continuing imminent threats.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: All of this—stopping foreign fighters, blocking terrorist financing, doing battle in cyberspace—is vital to the war against ISIS, but it also lays the foundation for defusing and defeating the next threat and the one after that.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: Now, the third element of our strategy has to be hardening our defenses at home and helping our partners do the same against both external and home-grown threats.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: After 9/11, the United States made a lot of progress breaking down bureaucratic barriers to allow for more and better information sharing among agencies responsible for keeping us safe.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: We still have work to do on this front, but by comparison, Europe is way behind.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: Today, European nations don't even always alert each other when they turn away a suspected jihadist at the border, or when a passport is stolen.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: It seems like after most terrorist attacks, we find out that the perpetrators were known to some security service or another, but too often the dots never get connected.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: I appreciate how hard this is, especially given the sheer number of suspects and threats, but this has to change.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: The United States must work with Europe to dramatically and immediately improve intelligence sharing and counterterrorism coordination.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: European countries also should have the flexibility to enhance their border controls when circumstances warrant.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: And here at home, we face a number of our own challenges.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: The threat to airline security is evolving as terrorists develop new devices like nonmetallic bombs.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: So our defenses have to stay at least one step ahead.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: We know that intelligence gathered and shared by local law enforcement officers is absolutely critical to breaking up plots and preventing attacks.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: So they need all the resources and support we can give them.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: Law enforcement also needs the trust of residents and communities, including in our own country Muslim Americans.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: Now, this should go without saying, but in the current climate, it bears repeating.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: Muslim Americans are working every day on the front lines of the fight against radicalization.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: Another challenge is how to strike the right balance of protecting privacy and security.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: Encryption of mobile communications presents a particularly tough problem.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: We should take the concerns of law enforcement and counterterrorism professionals seriously.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: They have warned that impenetrable encryption may prevent them from accessing terrorist communications and preventing a future attack.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: On the other hand, we know there are legitimate concerns about government intrusion, network security, and creating new vulnerabilities that bad actors can and would exploit.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: So we need Silicon Valley not to view government as its adversary.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: Now is the time to solve this problem, not after the next attack.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: Since Paris, no homeland security challenge is being more hotly debated than how to handle Syrian refugees seeking safety in the United States.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: Our highest priority, of course, must always be protecting the American people.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: So yes, we do need to be vigilant in screening and vetting any refugees from Syria, guided by the best judgment of our security professionals, in close coordination with our allies and partners.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: And Congress need to make sure the necessary resources are provided for comprehensive background checks, drawing on the best intelligence we can get.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: And we should be taking a close look at the safeguards in the visa programs as well, but we cannot allow terrorists to intimidate us into abandoning our values and our humanitarian obligations.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: Turning away orphans, applying a religious test, discriminating against Muslims, slamming the door on every Syrian refugee, that is just not who we are.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: We are better than that.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: And remember, many of these refugees are fleeing the same terrorists who threaten us.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: It would be a cruel irony indeed if ISIS can force families from their homes and then also prevent them from ever finding new ones.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: We should be doing more to ease this humanitarian crisis, not less.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: And we can get this right.

texte: America's open, free, tolerant society is described by some as a vulnerability in the struggle against terrorism, but I actually believe it's one of our strengths.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: It reduces the appeal of radicalism and enhances the richness and resilience of our communities.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: This is not a time for scoring political points.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: When New York was attacked on 9/11, we had a Republican president, a Republican governor and a Republican mayor, and I worked with all of them.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: We pulled together and put partisanship aside to rebuild our city and protect our country.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City
texte: This is a time for American leadership.

texte: No other country can rally the world to defeat ISIS and win the generational struggle against radical jihadism.

titre: Remarks and a Question and Answer Session at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York City

texte: There's been a lot of talk lately about coalitions.

texte: But in the Twin Cities, you have also seen firsthand how communities come together to resist radicalization: local imams condemning terrorist violence, local artists and activists pushing back against terrorist propaganda.

texte: So we need to pursue all of them at once, using every pillar of American power.

texte: I've watched this a long time.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: And I have always thought that given the unpredictability and the, you know, changes in people's concerns going into this election, that we wouldn't know exactly how the outcome would be for, you know, a couple of cycles of these primaries and caucuses.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: So, I'm going to do my best to convince more Iowans to come out and caucus for me.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: Well, the Vice President who I deeply respect and regard as a friend, went on to say as I recall.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: I was a legal services lawyer defending poor people.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: I went to work to try to make sure that we got health care in the beginning of my husband's administration because of so many people who were left out and were uninsured.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: I have been on this issue in many different ways.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: How do we make education more equal?

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: How do we make health care more equal?

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: Of course that's tied to income equality, but there is also a broader range of issues that I have a long record of addressing.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: And when I was in the Senate I took on corporate executive pay.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: A lot of the abuses that I thought were there.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: I took on these derivatives and credit default swaps that contributed to the collapse of the economy and the great recession.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: I stood up to Wall Street.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: So I have a very long record.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: I have a broader agenda.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: It's not the only thing I talk about because I think you have to view equality of opportunity and how we deliver that in the 21st Century for many different perspectives and that's what I tried to do.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: But you know, I have a lot of regard for the vice president.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: And I think today he clarified what he said and said he was talking about me when I was Secretary of State.

texte: There is an unwritten rule, you do not meddle in domestic policy when you are secretary of state or for that matter, secretary of defense.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: So yes, for four years, despite a long career both in and out of public service where I have been relentless in talking about these issues, there were four years when I did not.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: I talked about how we were going to get Iran to the negotiating table and try to prevent them from getting a nuclear weapon, how we're going to, you know, deal with a rising China, what we're going to do about women's rights, something that goes to the heart of inequality.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: So, I had a different agenda because I had a different job.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: Well, we've got a variety of proposals.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: Not only the four percent surcharge which I call the fair share surcharge.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: The so-called Buffet Rule which would have a minimum tax rate for people making more than $1 million, limiting deductions to 28 percent with a charitable exception.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: Going after a lot of the subsidies that, for example, still subsidize the oil and gas industry about $6 billion a year while we have to move toward a clean renewable energy future.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: So I have put forth plans, paid family leave, tuition, debt-free tuition for public colleges.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: Capping prescription drug costs and much more.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: And it would cost about $100 billion a year, all of which I pay for.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: And he had promised that he would roll out his tax plans before the Iowa caucus on February 1st.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: Well, if you wait too long, nobody will have a chance to see them or analyze them.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: And so I am very clear about what I would do and how I would pay for it.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: This is a very big difference in this campaign.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: Because as you saw, I received the Brady campaign endorsement today and both the woman Delfin Cherry who introduced us to the stage and the head of the Brady campaign had lost family members.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: It was really hard standing up there because I have held the hands of and listened to countless people who have lost family members to gun violence.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: And I agree completely with the President about us having to take action now.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: We lose on an average 90 people a day.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: It has to stop, Alisyn.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: I've been in this campaign advocating for comprehensive background checks, closing the gun show loophole, closing the online loophole, closing what's called the Charleston loophole.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: You know, there was a loophole, my opponent voted for it, Senator Sanders, that at the end of three days, business days, you get that gun whether they have finished the background check or not.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: The killer in Charleston who bought that gun, if there had just been a little more time, it would have been discovered he should not have been able to buy the gun because he had a federal record.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: We have saved a lot of lives.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: I can't put an exact number on it.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: But because of the Brady bill which Senator Sanders voted against five times, more than two million people, the Brady campaign says, 2.4 million purchasers have been stopped from buying guns.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: So, we are talking about violent criminals.

texte: We are talking about domestic abusers.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: We are talking about the dangerously mentally ill. We are even talking about terrorists because the Republicans won't close the loophole so that people on the no fly zone can buy guns.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: I feel passionately about this.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: And the cumulation from Sandy Hook to the community college in Oregon, the fact that we have so many mass killings in the last few years, I think it certainly motivated the President, and I am so proud to support him and I want to make this a voting issue in this campaign.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: I'm going to let him say whatever he wants to say.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: He can run his campaign however he wishes.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: I'm going to keep talking about what the next president will have to do starting January 20th, 2017.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: I have deep disagreements with what he's proposing.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: His tax plans would cut trillions of dollars of taxes from the wealthy and corporations.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: He doesn't believe in equal pay.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: He thinks that American workers are already making too much.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: So, I'm going to draw the contrast with him that I think the American people are interested in seeing.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: I'm going to let the American voters decide what's relevant and what's not relevant in their decision as to who they're going to support.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: Yes, it would be amazing.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: I would look forward to it.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: Look, I think this is serious business.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: Campaigns always have some great stories and great characters.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: That's part of the political process.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: This is really serious business, who the next president is.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: We are either going to build on the progress that we've made or we're going to see it ripped away.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: We are either going to defend human rights and civil rights and women's rights and gay rights and voting rights and workers' rights and all the rest that is at stake, or we are going to turn the clock back.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: And that's why I have tried to very clearly explain where I stand on all of these issues because the stakes are so high.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: And if I'm fortunate enough to get the nomination, I will run hard against whomever the Republicans' nominee, because they represent a brand of politics and policies that I think would hurt our country.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: I don't want to see that happen.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: Yes, let's say that.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: Well, I think the very first phone call would be to whoever I've asked to be the chief of staff of the White House.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: Let's get a meeting together, let's get our agenda together.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: There's a lot we have to get going.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: The earlier we start, the better we'll be off and we'll get more accomplished.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: Because I want to really think hard if I do get the nomination, right then and there, how we organize the White House, how we organize the cabinet.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: What's the legislative agenda?

texte: You know, the time between an election and inauguration is short.

texte: I mean, you can't take anything for granted.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: You have to keep working as hard as you possibly can, but I think it's important to start planning because we know what happens if you get behind in getting your agenda out and getting your appointments made.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: And you're not doing the work that the American people elected you to do.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: Well, she's right, because I feel very fortunate.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: I like to point out I'm the granddaughter of a factory worker who came to this country as a young immigrant.

texte: Went to work in the lace mills in Scranton, Pennsylvania.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: So, here I am three generations later asking people to vote for me to become their president.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: And we have this amazing 15-month-old grandchild with another on the way next summer.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: And so, I think a lot about the future, but I think not just about her future because we're going to do everything we can to make sure she has the best opportunities life can offer, but I think about what kind of country she'll become an adult in and what kind of world is going to be waiting for her.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: I want to make sure—it's not just our grandchild, but every child who has the opportunity to go as far to fulfill their God-given potential as possible.

titre: Interview with Alisyn Camerota of CNN
texte: And I want to be the president who unleashes that potential again.

texte: I'm always hopeful, Alisyn.

texte: I think this is the greatest country.
