titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: Thank you for the opportunity to speak with you.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: Today, I'm going to outline a plan for American economic revival – it is a bold, ambitious, forward-looking plan to massively increase jobs, wages, incomes and opportunities for the people of our country.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: My plan will embrace the truth that people flourish under a minimum government burden, and it will tap into the incredible unrealized potential of our workers and their dreams.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: Right now, 92 million Americans are on the sidelines, outside the workforce, and not part of our economy.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: It's a silent nation of jobless Americans.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: Look no further than the city of Flint, where I just visited.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: The jobs have stripped from this community, and its infrastructure has collapsed.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: In 1970, there were more than 80,000 people in Flint working for GM – today it is less than 8,000.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: Now Ford has announced it is moving all small car production to Mexico.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: It used to be cars were made in Flint and you couldn't drink the water in Mexico.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: Now, the cars are made in Mexico and you can't drink the water in Flint.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: We are going to turn this around.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: My economic plan rejects the cynicism that says our labor force will keep declining, that our jobs will keep leaving, and that our economy can never grow as it did once before.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: We reject the pessimism that says our standard of living can no longer rise, and that all that's left to do is divide up and redistribute our shrinking resources.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: Everything that is broken today can be fixed, and every failure can be turned into a great success.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: Jobs can stop leaving our country, and start pouring in.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: Failing schools can become flourishing schools.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: Crumbling roads and bridges can become gleaming new infrastructure.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: Inner cities can experience a flood of new jobs and investment.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: And rising crime can give way to safe and prosperous communities.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: All of these things, and so much more, are possible.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: But to accomplish them, we must replace the present policy of globalism – which has moved so many jobs and so much wealth out of our country – and replace it with a new policy of Americanism.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: Under this American System, every policy decision we make must pass a simple test: does it create more jobs and better wages for Americans?

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: If we lower our taxes, remove destructive regulations, unleash the vast treasure of American energy, and negotiate trade deals that put America First, then there is no limit to the number of jobs we can create and the amount of prosperity we can unleash.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: America will truly be the greatest place in the world to invest, hire, grow and to create new jobs, new technologies, and entire new industries.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: Instead of driving jobs and wealth away, America will become the world's great magnet for innovation and job creation.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: My opponent's plan rejects this optimism.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: She offers only more taxing, regulating, more spending and more wealth redistribution – a future of slow growth, declining incomes, and dwindling prosperity.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: The only people who get rich under Hillary Clinton's scheme are the donors and the special interests.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: In Hillary Clinton's America, we have surrendered our status as the world's great economy, and we have surrendered our middle class to the whims of foreign countries.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: Not one single idea she has will create one net American job, or create one new dollar of American wealth for our workers.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: The only thing she can ever offer is a welfare check.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: Our plan will produce paychecks, and they're going to be great paychecks for millions of people now unemployed.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: In the course of this campaign, I have travelled all across this country and I've met the most amazing people.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: Every day, I've seen the goodness and character of our country, and brave citizens proudly fighting through hard times and difficult circumstances.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: In many parts of our country, the hard times never seem to end.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: I've visited cities and towns in upstate New York where half the jobs have left and moved to other countries.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: Politicians have abandoned these places all over our country and the people who live there.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: Worse still, politicians have heaped scorn and disdain on these wonderful Americans.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: My opponent described tens of millions of American citizens as deplorable and irredeemable – how can Hillary Clinton seek to lead this country when she considers its citizens beyond redemption?

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: The hardworking people she calls deplorable are the most admirable people I know: they are cops and soldiers, teachers and firefighters, young and old, moms and dads, blacks, whites and Latinos – but above everything else, they are all American.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: They love their families, they love their country, and they want a better future.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: These are the forgotten men and women of America.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: People who work hard but don't have a voice.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: I am running to be their voice, and to fight to bring prosperity to every part of this country.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: Too many of our leaders have forgotten that it's their duty to protect the jobs, wages and well-being of American workers before any other consideration.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: I'm not running to be President of the world.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: I'm running to be President of the United States – and as your President, I will fight for every last American job.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: We are the nation that tamed the West, dug out the Panama Canal, won two World Wars, and put a man on the moon.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: It's time to start thinking big once again.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: That's why I believe it is time to establish a national goal of reaching 4% economic growth.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: In working with my economic team, we've put together a plan that puts us on track to achieve that goal.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: Over the next ten years, our economic team estimates that under our plan the economy will average 3.5% growth and create a total of 25 million new jobs.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: You can visit our website to see the math.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: This growth means that our jobs plan, including our childcare reforms, will be completely paid-for in combination with proposed budget savings.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: It will be deficit neutral.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: If we reach 4% growth, it will reduce the deficit.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: It will be accomplished through a complete overhaul of our tax, regulatory, energy and trade policies.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: Right now, under Obama-Clinton policies, the economy grew only 1.1 percent last quarter – that translates to millions of lost jobs.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: This is the weakest so-called recovery since the Great Depression.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: Over the last 7 years, the economy grew only 2.1 percent, the slowest period in seventy years.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: Had the economy grown under Obama at the same rate as Reagan, it would have meant 10 million more jobs.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: Perhaps most shockingly, 1 in 6 men aged 18-34 are either in jail or out of work.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: Meanwhile, another 2 million Hispanic-Americans have been added to the ranks of those in poverty.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: On top of it all, the Obama-Clinton policies have doubled the national debt.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: It took more than 230 years for the United States to accumulate it's first $10 trillion dollars in debt – it took President Obama only eight years to add another $10 trillion.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: Now, it would be one thing if that money had been used to completely rebuild our nation, our military, and our infrastructure.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: Instead, the opposite happened.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: We doubled our debt and, in return, we have dilapidated infrastructure, failing schools, a badly depleted military, and another 14 million people who have left the workforce.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: Never has so much money been spent so poorly.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: But we're going to turn that all around.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: It begins with bold new tax reform.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: As outlined in Detroit, our tax plan will greatly simplify the code and reduce the number of brackets from 7 to 3.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: The 3 new brackets will be 12, 25 and 33, but low-income Americans will pay no income tax at all – in fact, our plan will remove millions and millions of workers from the income tax rolls entirely.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: By lowering rates, streamlining deductions, and simplifying the process, we will add millions of new jobs.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: In addition, because we have strongly capped deductions for the wealthy and closed special interest loopholes, the tax relief will be concentrated on the working and middle class taxpayer.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: They will receive the biggest benefit – it won't even be close.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: This is a working and middle class tax relief proposal.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: The tax relief for these workers will be expanded by my childcare proposals that I have worked on with my daughter, Ivanka.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: These proposals are a central element of our comprehensive tax reform and economic growth plan.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: Families will be able to fully deduct the average cost of childcare from their taxes, including stay-at-home parents.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: Because this deduction is capped, it will disproportionately benefit working and middle class families.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: The less you make, the larger a share of your income you can exclude from taxation.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: Parents will also be able to enroll in tax-free dependent care savings accounts for their children or elderly relatives.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: Low-income households will benefit from both an Expanded Earned Income Tax Credit – in the form a Childcare rebate – and a matching $500 contribution for their savings accounts.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: A married couple earning $50,000 per year with two children and $8,000 in child care expenses will save 35% from their current tax bill.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: A married couple earning $75,000 per year with two children and $10,000 in child care expenses will receive a 30% reduction in their tax bill.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: By contrast, someone earning $5 million will receive virtually no change in their tax bill at all.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: One of our greatest job creation measures is going to be our 15% business tax rate – down from the current 35% rate, a reduction of more than 40 percent.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: An explosion of new business and new jobs will be created.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: It will be amazing to watch.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: We will also allow U.S.-based manufacturers to fully expense the cost of new plants and equipment.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: On top of that, we will bring back trillions in business wealth parked overseas and tax it at a 10% rate.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: Some people say there are $2 trillion dollars overseas, I think it's $5 trillion.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: By taxing it at 10% instead of 35%, all of this money will come back into our country.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: We will turn America into a magnet for new jobs – and that means jobs in our poorest communities.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: Next, comes regulations.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: One of the keys to unlocking growth is scaling-back years of disastrous regulations unilaterally imposed by our out-of-control bureaucracy.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: Regulations have grown into a massive, job-killing industry – and the regulation industry is one business I will put an end to.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: In 2015 alone, federal agencies issued over 3,300 final rules and regulations, up from 2,400 the prior year.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: Every year, overregulation costs our economy $2 trillion dollars a year and reduces household wealth by almost $15,000 dollars.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: I've proposed a moratorium on new federal regulations that are not compelled by Congress or public safety, and I will eliminate all needless and job-killing regulations now on the books.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: This includes eliminating some of our most intrusive regulations, like the Waters of The U.S. Rule.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: It also means scrapping the EPA's so-called Clean Power Plan which the government itself estimates will cost $7.2 billion a year.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: This Obama-Clinton directive will shut down most, if not all, coal-powered electricity plans in America.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: Remember what Hillary Clinton said?

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: She wants to shut down the miners, just like she wants to shut down the steel mills.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: We're going to put our great miners and steel workers back to work.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: Energy reform is central to our plan as well According to the Heritage Foundation, by 2030, President Obama's energy restrictions will eliminate another half a million manufacturing jobs, reduce economic output by $2.5 trillion dollars, and reduce incomes by $7,000 dollars per person.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: Hillary Clinton wants to go even further, and her plan could cost the economy $5 trillion dollars.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: A Trump Administration will lift restrictions on all sources of American energy production.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: According to the Institute for American Energy Resources this will: increase GDP by more than $100 billion annually add over 500,000 new jobs annually increase annual wages by more than $30 billion over the next 7 years increase federal, state, and local tax revenues by almost $6 trillion over 4 decades increase total economic activity by more than $20 trillion over the next 40 years.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: In addition, we will streamline the permitting process for all energy infrastructure projects, including the billions of dollars in projects held up by President Obama – creating countless more jobs in the process.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: Finally, comes trade – the foundation for everything America's annual trade deficit with the world is now nearly $800 a billion a year – an enormous drag on growth.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: Between World War II and the year 2000, the United States averaged a 3.5% growth rate.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: But, after China joined the World Trade Organization, our average growth rate has been reduced to only 2 percent.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: Predatory trade practices, product dumping, currency manipulation and intellectual property theft have taken millions of jobs and trillions in wealth from our country.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: It is no great secret that many of the special interests funding my opponent's campaign are the same people profiting from these terrible trade deals.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: The same so-called experts advising Hillary Clinton are the same people who gave us NAFTA, China's entry into the World Trade Organization, the job-killing trade deal with South Korea, and now the Trans-Pacific Partnership.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: All of the special interests that the media race to for comment have been proven wrong about every single deal they've promoted – every lie and every prediction has crashed upon the rocks of reality.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: Our manufacturing base has crumbled, communities have been hollowed out, wages have declined, and households are making less today than they were in the year 2000.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: I have proposed a detailed plan to reform our trade policies and bring vast new jobs and wealth to America.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: This includes the following steps: I'm going to direct the Secretary of Commerce to identify every violation of trade agreements a foreign country is currently using to harm our workers.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: I will use every tool under American and international law to end these abuses, and I will use our greatest business leaders and finest negotiators – and I know who you are, many of you are in the room.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: We are going to start with NAFTA, which is causing so much damage to our country.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: We will entirely renegotiate NAFTA into a deal that will either be good for us or will be terminated until a brand new and productive deal can be signed.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: We are also going to keep America out of the Trans-Pacific Partnership.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: Next, I am going to instruct my Treasury Secretary to label China a currency manipulator, and to apply tariffs to any country that devalues its currency to gain an unfair advantage over the United States.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: I am going to instruct the U.S. Trade Representative to bring trade cases against China.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: China's unfair subsidy behavior is prohibited by the terms of its entrance to the WTO, and I intend to enforce those rules.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: If China does not stop its illegal activities, including its theft of American trade secrets and intellectual property, I will apply countervailing duties until China ceases and desists.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: Just the single action of enforcing intellectual property rules alone would add millions of new American jobs.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: According to the U.S. International Trade Commission, improved protection of America's intellectual property in China would add 2 million jobs a year to the United States every single year.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: We are going to stop the outflow of jobs from our country, and open a new highway of jobs back into our country.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: Here is how the plan adds up We are proposing a $4.4 trillion tax cut that will score as $2.6 trillion under a dynamic growth model, which is how taxes should be scored.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: This includes the childcare plan.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: Our economic team has further modeled that the growth-induced savings from trade, energy and regulation reform will shave at least another $1.8 trillion off of the remaining cost.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: That leaves around $800 billion dollars.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: This money can all be saved through simple, common sense reforms.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: If we save just one penny of each federal dollar spent on non-defense, and non-entitlement programs, we can save almost $1 trillion over the next decade – again this is spending that does not touch defense, and that does not touch entitlements.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: If our plan exceeds the 3.5% ten-year growth average, then our jobs proposal will actually reduce the deficit.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: Savings will be compounded by the fact that people who are currently receiving unemployment or welfare will finally be able to find jobs.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: This is the most pro-growth, pro-jobs, pro-family plan put forth perhaps in the history of our country.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City
texte: This is what our new future will look like I am going to lower you taxes; I am going to get rid of massive amounts of unnecessary regulations, on business and in your life; I'm going to unleash American energy; I'm going to repeal and replace Obamacare; I'm going to appoint Justices to the Supreme Court who will follow the Constitution; I'm going rebuild our depleted military and take care of our vets; I'm going to save your 2nd amendment; I'm going to stop illegal immigration and drugs coming into our country, and yes, we will build the wall ; and I'm going to renegotiate our disastrous trade deals, especially NAFTA – and we will only make great trade deals that put the American worker first.

titre: Remarks to the Economic Club of New York at the Waldorf Astoria in New York City

titre: Remarks at a Rally at the James L. Knight Center in Miami, Florida
texte: My first day in office, I am going to order a review of every single regulation issued over the last eight years.

titre: Remarks at a Rally at the James L. Knight Center in Miami, Florida
texte: All needless, job-killing regulations will be cancelled.

titre: Remarks at a Rally at the James L. Knight Center in Miami, Florida
texte: Millions of new jobs will come pouring in.

titre: Remarks at a Rally at the James L. Knight Center in Miami, Florida
texte: We are going to lift the restrictions on American energy – which means at least another half a million new jobs a year.

titre: Remarks at a Rally at the James L. Knight Center in Miami, Florida
texte: That's just the beginning.

titre: Remarks at a Rally at the James L. Knight Center in Miami, Florida
texte: Also on my first day, I am going to ask Congress to send me a bill to immediately repeal and replace disastrous Obamacare – this will instantly save another 2 million jobs.

titre: Remarks at a Rally at the James L. Knight Center in Miami, Florida
texte: I am also going to completely reform our trade deals.

titre: Remarks at a Rally at the James L. Knight Center in Miami, Florida
texte: We are going to renegotiate NAFTA, stand up to China, and keep America out of the TPP.

titre: Remarks at a Rally at the James L. Knight Center in Miami, Florida
texte: We don't need another massive multinational deal that ties us up and binds us down.

titre: Remarks at a Rally at the James L. Knight Center in Miami, Florida
texte: Another major reform is going to be school choice.

titre: Remarks at a Rally at the James L. Knight Center in Miami, Florida
texte: I've outlined a plan to provide every disadvantaged child in America the freedom to choose the private, public, magnet or religious school of his or her choice.

titre: Remarks at a Rally at the James L. Knight Center in Miami, Florida
texte: This will help lift millions of poor African-American and Hispanic children out of poverty.

titre: Remarks at a Rally at the James L. Knight Center in Miami, Florida
texte: Since President Obama came into office, another 2 million Hispanic-Americans have fallen into poverty.

titre: Remarks at a Rally at the James L. Knight Center in Miami, Florida
texte: This is unacceptable.

titre: Remarks at a Rally at the James L. Knight Center in Miami, Florida
texte: To the Hispanic community I say: we are going to protect your jobs, we are going to build up your schools, and we are going to deliver safety and opportunity for your children.

titre: Remarks at a Rally at the James L. Knight Center in Miami, Florida
texte: Earlier this week, I also rolled out a plan to help our mothers and our families get affordable, quality childcare for their children.

titre: Remarks at a Rally at the James L. Knight Center in Miami, Florida
texte: On policy after policy, we are going to provide opportunity, prosperity and security for all Americans.

titre: Remarks at a Rally at the James L. Knight Center in Miami, Florida
texte: We are also going to stand with the Cuban people in their fight against communist oppression.

titre: Remarks at a Rally at the James L. Knight Center in Miami, Florida
texte: The President's one-sided deal for Cuba benefits only the Castro Regime.

titre: Remarks at a Rally at the James L. Knight Center in Miami, Florida
texte: But all of the concessions that Barack Obama has granted the Castro Regime were done through executive order, which means the next President can reverse them – and that is what I will do, unless the Castro Regime meets our demands.

titre: Remarks at a Rally at the James L. Knight Center in Miami, Florida
texte: Those demands will include religious and political freedom for the Cuban people.

titre: Remarks at a Rally at the James L. Knight Center in Miami, Florida
texte: Let's also talk about Venezuela.

titre: Remarks at a Rally at the James L. Knight Center in Miami, Florida
texte: Venezuela is a beautiful, vibrant, and resource-rich country, filled with amazing and hardworking people.

titre: Remarks at a Rally at the James L. Knight Center in Miami, Florida
texte: But Venezuela has been run into the ground by socialists.

titre: Remarks at a Rally at the James L. Knight Center in Miami, Florida
texte: The next President of the United States must stand in solidarity with all people oppressed in our hemisphere, and I will stand with the oppressed people of Venezuela yearning to be free.

titre: Remarks at a Rally at the James L. Knight Center in Miami, Florida
texte: Here, in America, I will push to expand freedom for all of our people.

titre: Remarks at a Rally at the James L. Knight Center in Miami, Florida
texte: I am going to lower you taxes; I am going to get rid of massive amounts of unnecessary regulations, on business and in your life; I'm going to repeal and replace Obamacare; I'm going to appoint Justices to the Supreme Court who will follow the Constitution; I'm going to rebuild our depleted military and take care of our vets; I'm going to save your 2nd amendment; I'm going to stop illegal immigration and drugs coming into our country, and yes, we will build the wall and I'm going to renegotiate our disastrous trade deals, especially NAFTA – and we will make great trade deals that put the American worker first.

titre: Remarks at a Rally at the James L. Knight Center in Miami, Florida
texte: We will rebuild our roads, bridges, tunnels, highways, airports, schools and hospitals.

titre: Remarks at a Rally at the James L. Knight Center in Miami, Florida
texte: American cars will travel the roads, American planes will soar in the skies, and American ships will patrol the seas.

titre: Remarks at a Rally at the James L. Knight Center in Miami, Florida
texte: American steel will send new skyscrapers into the clouds.

titre: Remarks at a Rally at the James L. Knight Center in Miami, Florida
texte: American hands will rebuild this nation – and American energy, mined from American sources, will power this nation.

titre: Remarks at a Rally at the James L. Knight Center in Miami, Florida
texte: American workers will be hired to do the job.

titre: Remarks at a Rally at the James L. Knight Center in Miami, Florida
texte: We will put new American steel into the spine of this country.

titre: Remarks at a Rally at the James L. Knight Center in Miami, Florida
texte: I will fight for every neglected part of this nation – and I will fight to bring us all together as One American People.

titre: Remarks at a Rally at the James L. Knight Center in Miami, Florida
texte: Imagine what our country could accomplish if we started working together as One People, under One God, saluting One American Flag.

titre: Remarks at a Rally at the James L. Knight Center in Miami, Florida
texte: It is time to break with the bitter failures of the past, and to embrace a new, inclusive and prosperous American future.

titre: Remarks at a Rally at the James L. Knight Center in Miami, Florida
texte: Jobs will return, incomes will rise, and new factories will come rushing back to our shores.

titre: Remarks at a Rally at the James L. Knight Center in Miami, Florida
texte: Once more, we will have a government of, by and for the people.

titre: Remarks at a Rally at the James L. Knight Center in Miami, Florida
texte: We Will Make America Prosperous Again.

titre: Remarks at a Rally at the James L. Knight Center in Miami, Florida
texte: We Will Make America Strong Again.

titre: Remarks at a Rally at the James L. Knight Center in Miami, Florida
texte: And Will Make America Great Again.

titre: Remarks at a Rally at the James L. Knight Center in Miami, Florida
texte: Thank you, and God Bless!

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: I thank you all for that warm welcome.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: There's nowhere I'd rather be than right here with all of you this morning.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: Please everyone be seated.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: This is such a great opportunity to lift up the work that so many of you have done for years -- your organizations, individually -- and I am grateful for it because it has helped to guide me in a lot of the work that I've been privileged to do.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: I want to thank Gwen Hess for her introduction.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: I want to acknowledge, it's always great to see a woman serve as president in any setting.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: I want to congratulate today's honorees.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: Everyone is so deserving of this recognition.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: I also want to acknowledge a few others.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: We have some fierce members of Congress with us today, women whom I admire, who have been my colleagues and friends and with whom I am looking forward to continuing our work: Congresswoman Sheila Jackson Lee, Congresswoman Gwen Moore, Congresswoman Yvette Clarke, Congresswoman Stacey Plaskett.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: And I want to give a special shout out to Congresswoman Joyce Beatty.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: When I saw Joyce recently, she said, 'Well, you are coming, aren't you?'

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: And I said, 'I'm working hard to get it set.'

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: And I am so proud that it did work out, and I thank Joyce for that extra push.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: I also want to acknowledge someone who had such a profound effect on my life, in every way, someone whom I admire and love, Marian Wright Edelman.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: This audience is filled with longtime friends and people I went to Wellesley College with that became life-long friends to me, and so many of you who have been on the front lines -- everyone associated with The Black Women's Agenda, I'm thrilled to be with you.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: I'm thrilled to be associated with you.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: I'm also thrilled to be back on the campaign trail.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: As the world knows, I was a little under the weather recently.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: The good news is, my pneumonia finally got some Republicans interested in women's health.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: Looking back, I know, I should have followed my doctor's orders to rest, but, my instinct was to push through it.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: That is what women do every single day, and I felt no different.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: Life has shown us that we do have to work harder at the office while still bearing most of the responsibilities at home -- that we always need to keep going because our families and our communities count on us.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: And I think it is more than fair to say, that black women have an even tougher road.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: And you, your daughters, your granddaughters -- I was pleased to meet Gwen's beautiful granddaughter earlier -- leave the house every morning, put on that game face that we all practice, and enter a society that consistently challenges your worth.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: With the images you see, the lower pay that so many take home, that try to silence your voices and break your spirits; yet, you remain fierce in the face of these challenges.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: We see that every day in the businesses you start, the art you create, the children you teach and the communities and organizations you lead.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: While your stories are often missing from the history books -- make no mistake -- you are the change makers, the path breakers, and the ground shakers.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: And, you are proof that yes, indeed, black girl magic is real.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: Now, I've been blessed to see this magic's influence on kids and communities up close for decades, starting with my first job after law school working with Marian at the Children's Defense Fund.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: Marian's belief was that every single child had worth and potential and deserved the opportunity to live up to their god potential with the tools and the support that every child needs.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: And that if we just improve the odds a bit for those suffering in poverty, they could flourish.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: So she led our team into some very poor communities.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: We met kids who had dropped out of school because they couldn't afford textbooks or transportation.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: Some didn't have decent clothes and stayed home to avoid being humiliated in class.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: Some had untreated medical and dental problems that made it practically impossible for them to learn.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: Those stories really hurt my heart.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: But Marian always believed we could deliver help and hope if we never ever gave up.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: So she taught us ways to think creatively, as well as strategically-- to take our advocacy and turn it into action and results.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: She sent me to New Bedford, Massachusetts, to go door to door looking for children who weren't in school.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: That was back before we had a legal requirement that every child, regardless of disability, deserved to get an education.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: I met a young girl in New Bedford and sat and talked with her on the small back porch of her house.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: She told me how badly she wanted to learn, but couldn't because schools weren't accessible or welcoming.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: So Marian had us get to work and change that.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: We gathered evidence and built a coalition.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: We helped convince Congress to ensure access to education for all students with disabilities.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: Marian showed me that to drive real progress, you have to change both hearts and laws.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: You need both understanding and action.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: And there is no question, I'm here today because of her example.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: I also want to recognize pioneers like Barbara Jordan and Shirley Chisholm, who sacrificed and struggled so that I and so many other women running for office could soar.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: I'm here because of friends and colleagues, like Donna Brazile, Reverend Leah Daugherty and Congresswoman Marcia Fudge — three black women who ran the Democratic National Convention in July.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: It was a great four days.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: It goes to show that black women deserve more than a seat at the table.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: It's past time you had a fair chance to run the meeting.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: And let's be clear: I would not be the Demo-cratic nominee for President of the United States were it not for black women like all of you who made noise at the polls this year in support of our campaign -- who did surrogate events, went to barber shops and beauty salons and cafes, got on local radio and local TV to make the case.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: We've come far together.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: And as I said yesterday in North Carolina, I'm going to close my campaign the way I began my career all those years ago at the Children's Defense Fund, and the way that I will serve as your president should I have the great honor of being elected: I will be focused on opportunities for kids and fairness for families.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: The American people deserve something to vote for, not just against.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: And together -- together, we are going to make this a freer, fairer and stronger nation.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: We're going to fight for the parents struggling to balance family and work and push for affordable child care, paid family leave, and yes, finally, equal pay for women.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: We'll fight for the young girls who want a fair chance in life, which is why we'll make universal pre-k available so that every child -- no matter what they look like or where they live -- can rise up and be prepared to fulfill their academic destiny.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: We are also going to do a lot to emphasize STEM education, particularly for girls and women, and I thank the agenda for making that a priority!

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: We'll fight for the entrepreneur who said that more businesses die in the parking lots of banks than anywhere else, which is why we're going to increase access to capital, and we are going to help African American women continue to represent the fastest growing segment of women-owned businesses in America right now.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: We are going to invest in communities that have been left out and left behind.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: Urban reinvestment and restructuring that is going to give more people decent housing, access to jobs, the transportation to get to those jobs, rural communities that are too often ignored and denied the services they need.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: I am a fan of Jim Clyburn's '10-20-30' plan.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: I am going to do everything I can to push that forward.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: We'll remember the pain of the Mothers of the Movement and fight for a criminal justice system that actually delivers justice and a future where everyone has respect for the law and is respected by the law.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: And we are going to pass common-sense reforms to keep guns out of the hands of dangerous people and keep our communities safe.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: We'll remember the families neglected in Flint and take action so that no child's life is ever put at risk again when brushing their teeth or drinking a glass of water at din-ner.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: We'll advocate for everyone concerned about their parents and grandparents as they age, and lift up caregivers and home care workers so older Americans can live in comfort and with dignity.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: And we're going to protect and enhance Social Security, which is the main source of income for older women.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: We'll stand-by-side to make sure that all of our rights are respected and protected – civil rights and women's rights, LGBT rights, worker's rights and, of course, voting rights.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: We are coming together at a pivotal moment for our country.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: Now I do believe that every election is important.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: But this one feels different, doesn't it?

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: That's because it is.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: The next 53 days will shape the next 50 years.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: The future of our children and grandchildren hangs in the balance.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: On one hand, we have my opponent, Donald Trump, and in recent weeks, he's tried to restrain himself and clean up his image.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: But as Maya Angelou once said, 'When some-one shows you who they are, believe them the first time.'

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: And we know who Donald is.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: For five years, he has led the birther movement to de-legitimize our first black president.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: His campaign was founded on this outrageous lie.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: There is no erasing it in history.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: Just yesterday, Trump again refused to say with his own words that the president was born in the United States.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: Donald's advisors had the temerity to say, 'He's doing the country a 'service' by pushing these lies.'

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: He's feeding into the worst im-pulses -- the bigotry and bias -- that lurks in our country.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: Barack Obama was born in America, plain and simple.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: And Donald Trump owes him and the American people an apology.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: So, my friends, there is no 'new' Donald Trump.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: There never will be.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: Donald Trump looks at President Obama after eight years as our president.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: He still doesn't see him as an American.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: Think of how dangerous that is.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: Imagine a person in the Oval Office who traffics in conspiracy theories and refuses to let them go – no matter what the facts are.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: Imagine someone who distorts the truth to fit a very narrow view of the world.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: Imagine a president who sees someone who doesn't look like him, and doesn't agree with him, and thinks, 'That person must not be a real American.'

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: Donald Trump is unfit to be President of the United States.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: We cannot become insensitive to what he says and what he stirs up.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: We can't just accept this.We've got to stand up to it.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: If we don't, it won't stop.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: In addition to the president, Donald Trump looks at a distinguished federal judge, born in Indiana, and he sees a Mexican, not an American.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: He looks at a Gold Star family and sees them as Muslims, not patriotic Americans.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: He looks at women and decides how our looks rate on a scale of one to 10.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: I look at America, I see everyone.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: I see our great diversity, which is one of our core strengths, not our burden.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: We know who Donald Trump is.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: Now it's time for our country to show who we are and reject his divisive vision.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: That's why this election is so important.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: As Michelle Obama said at the Democratic Convention, 'When we go to the polls this November, the real choice isn't between a Democrat or Republican.'

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: It's about who will have the power to shape our children's lives for the next four years.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: It's also about the kind of country we want to be, and what we want to leave behind for future generations.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: We are at our best when every person gets to share in our nation's promise, contribute to its progress.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: 'Stronger Together' is not just our campaign slogan.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: It's the guiding principle for the future we need to build.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: So Americans, we need to ask themselves: Are we going to make our economy work for everyone or just for those at the top?

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: Are we going to bring people together or pit Americans against each other and rip our country apart?

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: Are we going to work with our allies to keep us safe or are we going to put a loose cannon in charge who would risk everything that generations of Americans have worked so hard to build?

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: Now in many ways, the profound choice is up to the women in this room.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: African American women turned out to vote more than any other group of Americans in 2012.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: This year, once again, you have your hands on the wheel of history and you can write the next chapter of the American story.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: Keep up the great work with your Four for 4' campaign.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: Make sure we get as many people registered and then to the polls as we possibly can.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: People say to me all time, 'I just -- I don't know what to do about Trump and his supporters and the things he says and inciting violence and all of the terrible activities that are happening this election year.'

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.
texte: Well, here's what we can do.

titre: Remarks to the Black Women's Agenda Symposium in Washington, D.C.

titre: Debate between Trump and Clinton

texte: But we've got to get costs down.

texte: We've got to provide additional help to small businesses so that they can afford to provide health insurance.

titre: Debate between Trump and Clinton

titre: Debate between Trump and Clinton
texte: So I want us to get to 100 percent, but get costs down and keep quality up.

titre: Debate between Trump and Clinton
texte: And it's very clear.

titre: Debate between Trump and Clinton

titre: Debate between Trump and Clinton

titre: Debate between Trump and Clinton

titre: Debate between Trump and Clinton

titre: Debate between Trump and Clinton
texte: So let's fix what's broken about it, but let's not throw it away and give it all back to the insurance companies and the drug companies.

titre: Debate between Trump and Clinton

texte: And I've heard this question from a lot of Muslim-Americans across our country, because, unfortunately, there's been a lot of very divisive, dark things said about Muslims.

titre: Debate between Trump and Clinton

titre: Debate between Trump and Clinton

titre: Debate between Trump and Clinton

titre: Debate between Trump and Clinton
texte: I will be the president and we will get it done.

texte: That's exactly right.

texte: And there is a determined effort by the Russian air force to destroy Aleppo in order to eliminate the last of the Syrian rebels who are really holding out against the Assad regime.

titre: Debate between Trump and Clinton
texte: Russia hasn't paid any attention to ISIS.

titre: Debate between Trump and Clinton
texte: They're interested in keeping Assad in power.

titre: Debate between Trump and Clinton
texte: So I, when I was secretary of state, advocated and I advocate today a no-fly zone and safe zones.

texte: We need some leverage with the Russians, because they are not going to come to the negotiating table for a diplomatic resolution, unless there is some leverage over them.

texte: And we have to work more closely with our partners and allies on the ground.

texte: But I want to emphasize that what is at stake here is the ambitions and the aggressiveness of Russia.

titre: Debate between Trump and Clinton
texte: Russia has decided that it's all in, in Syria.

titre: Remarks at the Kendall Campus of Miami Dade College in Miami, Florida
texte: It doesn't have a lot of special effects – but it does have a lot of drama.

titre: Remarks at the Kendall Campus of Miami Dade College in Miami, Florida
texte: And here's the main message: climate change is real, it's urgent, and America can take the lead in the world in addressing it.

titre: Remarks at the Kendall Campus of Miami Dade College in Miami, Florida
texte: We here in America can develop new clean energy solutions.

titre: Remarks at the Kendall Campus of Miami Dade College in Miami, Florida
texte: We can transform our economy.

texte: We can rally the world to cut carbon pollution.

titre: Remarks at the Kendall Campus of Miami Dade College in Miami, Florida
texte: And above all, we can fulfill our moral obligation to protect our planet for our children and our grandchildren.

titre: Remarks at the Kendall Campus of Miami Dade College in Miami, Florida
texte: Now, let me just say – so, so let's remember, let's remember what's at stake.

titre: Remarks at the Kendall Campus of Miami Dade College in Miami, Florida

texte: So this is something that Al Gore's been working on for a really long time.

titre: Remarks at the Kendall Campus of Miami Dade College in Miami, Florida
texte: It was in 1982 when he held the very first hearing on climate change in the House of Representatives with the world-famous climate scientist Jim Hansen.

titre: Remarks at the Kendall Campus of Miami Dade College in Miami, Florida
texte: And then when Al became a senator, he continued to raise the alarm and look for solutions, and as vice president, he led America's efforts to negotiate the Kyoto Protocol to cut greenhouse gas emissions.

titre: Remarks at the Kendall Campus of Miami Dade College in Miami, Florida
texte: You take all this together, those 30 years of leadership led Al Gore to be awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2007.

titre: Remarks at the Kendall Campus of Miami Dade College in Miami, Florida
texte: I was very proud because he had been determined and persistent, and in the face of a lot of people – in public life, in business, in elsewhere who were trying to diminish the importance of the science – he never wavered.

titre: Remarks at the Kendall Campus of Miami Dade College in Miami, Florida
texte: And in the years since, the climate challenge has only grown more stark.

titre: Remarks at the Kendall Campus of Miami Dade College in Miami, Florida
texte: And I will tell you this, it is one of the most important issues at stake in this election.

titre: Remarks at the Kendall Campus of Miami Dade College in Miami, Florida
texte: Look at it this way.

titre: Remarks at the Kendall Campus of Miami Dade College in Miami, Florida
texte: Our next president will either step up our efforts to address climate change, to protect our planet, to protect our health, and to create good jobs that cannot be outsourced by growing our clean energy economy.

texte: Or in the alternative, we will be dragged backwards and our whole future will be put at risk.

titre: Remarks at the Kendall Campus of Miami Dade College in Miami, Florida
texte: So we've really got to get this right.

texte: And if you need additional convincing, just remember what happened this week.

titre: Remarks at the Kendall Campus of Miami Dade College in Miami, Florida

titre: Remarks at the Kendall Campus of Miami Dade College in Miami, Florida
texte: We all need to support each other as our communities put the pieces back together and begin the long road back from this disaster.

texte: That's why I've encouraged everyone to give what you can afford to the Florida Disaster Fund or to Team Rubicon, the veterans organization working to respond to Hurricane Matthew, or to UNICEF, helping children and families on the ground in Haiti.

titre: Remarks at the Kendall Campus of Miami Dade College in Miami, Florida
texte: Now, some will say, 'We've always had hurricanes.

texte: But there's also health consequences.

texte: Mosquitoes that carry diseases like the Zika virus and ticks that carry Lyme disease are expanding their ranges.

texte: We cannot risk putting a climate denier in the White House.

texte: We need a president who believes in science and who has a plan to lead America in facing this threat, creating good jobs, and yes, saving our planet.

texte: So here's what I want to do.

texte: And I want you to be part of making it us.

texte: And we need to accelerate the transition to a clean energy economy and create high paying jobs, building and installing more solar panels and wind turbines.

titre: Remarks at the Kent State Student Recreation Center in Kent, Ohio
texte: Donald Trump is different.

titre: Remarks at the Kent State Student Recreation Center in Kent, Ohio
texte: That's as serious as it gets.

titre: Remarks at the Kent State Student Recreation Center in Kent, Ohio
texte: So today, I want to talk about our national security.

titre: Remarks at the Kent State Student Recreation Center in Kent, Ohio
texte: Because when the election is over and people wake up on November 9th, we will have picked the person who will carry the responsibility for all these weighty decisions.

titre: Remarks at the Kent State Student Recreation Center in Kent, Ohio

titre: Remarks at the Kent State Student Recreation Center in Kent, Ohio
texte: And I just want to focus on three of the most crucial questions facing the next President: Can you be trusted to command our nuclear arsenal and make literally life and death decisions about war and peace?

titre: Remarks at the Kent State Student Recreation Center in Kent, Ohio
texte: And do you know the difference between our allies and our adversaries?

titre: Remarks at the Kent State Student Recreation Center in Kent, Ohio
texte: We'll start with nuclear weapons.

titre: Remarks at the Kent State Student Recreation Center in Kent, Ohio
texte: Now, I know there are some who will say that any discussion of this topic could be fear-mongering, but I don't think so and in part of what you just heard from Bruce Blair.

titre: Remarks at the Kent State Student Recreation Center in Kent, Ohio
texte: When dozens of retired nuclear launch officers publicly state that Donald Trump should, and I quote, 'not have his finger on the button,' then this is a topic that can't be avoided.

titre: Remarks at the Kent State Student Recreation Center in Kent, Ohio
texte: And as I've said, Donald has repeatedly suggested that more countries should have nuclear weapons.

titre: Remarks at the Kent State Student Recreation Center in Kent, Ohio
texte: He must not realize or care that the more nuclear material there is in the world, the more likely terrorists are to get their hands on it -- or that someone will miscalculate and start a war that can't be stopped.

titre: Remarks at the Kent State Student Recreation Center in Kent, Ohio
texte: And when a few more countries go nuclear, their neighbors will feel pressure to do so as well.

titre: Remarks at the Kent State Student Recreation Center in Kent, Ohio
texte: One of the reasons I worked so hard to impose sanctions on Iran so that we could get them to the negotiating table was so we would not have a nuclear arms race in the Middle East and I am proud that we put a lid on Iran's nuclear weapons program.

titre: Remarks at the Kent State Student Recreation Center in Kent, Ohio
texte: But even the prospect of an actual nuclear war doesn't seem to bother Donald Trump.

titre: Remarks at the Kent State Student Recreation Center in Kent, Ohio
texte: 'Good luck, enjoy yourselves, folks,' was what he had to say about a potential nuclear conflict in Asia.

titre: Remarks at the Kent State Student Recreation Center in Kent, Ohio
texte: I wonder if he knows that a single nuclear warhead can kill millions of people.

titre: Remarks at the Kent State Student Recreation Center in Kent, Ohio
texte: These are weapons today far more powerful than the bombs that destroyed Hiroshima and Nagasaki during World War II.

titre: Remarks at the Kent State Student Recreation Center in Kent, Ohio

titre: Remarks at the Kent State Student Recreation Center in Kent, Ohio
texte: President Ronald Reagan once said -- and he worked hard for arms control and I admired what he did working with the Soviet Union -- and he once said he feared, and this is a quote from President Reagan, 'some fool or some maniac or some accident triggering the kind of war that is the end of the line for all of us.'

titre: Remarks at the Kent State Student Recreation Center in Kent, Ohio
texte: That has been the fear and the commitment of Democratic and Republican presidents since the dawn of the Atomic Age.

titre: Remarks at the Kent State Student Recreation Center in Kent, Ohio
texte: So what would he think about Donald Trump, who says he wants to be, and I quote, 'unpredictable' about using the most powerful weapons ever produced?

titre: Remarks at the Kent State Student Recreation Center in Kent, Ohio
texte: And here's the thing with nuclear weapons – as Bruce told you, when the President gives the order, that's it.

titre: Remarks at the Kent State Student Recreation Center in Kent, Ohio
texte: There's no veto for Congress, no veto by the Joint Chiefs.

titre: Remarks at the Kent State Student Recreation Center in Kent, Ohio
texte: The officers in the silos have no choice but to fire.

titre: Remarks at the Kent State Student Recreation Center in Kent, Ohio
texte: And that can take as little as four minutes.

titre: Remarks at the Kent State Student Recreation Center in Kent, Ohio
texte: That's why all those retired launch officers stepped forward and said Donald Trump should never be put in charge of our nuclear arsenal.

titre: Remarks at the Kent State Student Recreation Center in Kent, Ohio

texte: In 1973, Bruce was a young military officer working in an underground bunker in Montana.

titre: Remarks at the Kent State Student Recreation Center in Kent, Ohio

titre: Remarks at the Kent State Student Recreation Center in Kent, Ohio

titre: Remarks at the Kent State Student Recreation Center in Kent, Ohio

titre: Remarks at the Kent State Student Recreation Center in Kent, Ohio
texte: Then they waited for the final order from the President.

titre: Remarks at the Kent State Student Recreation Center in Kent, Ohio

titre: Remarks at the Kent State Student Recreation Center in Kent, Ohio
texte: But when Bruce looks at Donald Trump, and sees his hair-trigger temper, and he thinks about what it felt like inside that bunker that night.

titre: Remarks at the Kent State Student Recreation Center in Kent, Ohio

texte: When he's gotten a tough question from a reporter.

texte: That's why it was so upsetting to learn what Donald was actually doing on 9/11.

texte: And I will never forget the sight of Ground Zero.

texte: The thick smoke made it hard to breathe or see.

titre: Remarks at the Kent State Student Recreation Center in Kent, Ohio
texte: Some of the firefighters and other first responders we met had been on duty nonstop since the planes hit the towers.

titre: Remarks at the Kent State Student Recreation Center in Kent, Ohio
texte: They had all lost friends.

titre: Remarks at the Kent State Student Recreation Center in Kent, Ohio
texte: In a makeshift command center, we were briefed on the damage, and it was clear we were going to need a lot of help to recover New York, and we were going to have to really make it our absolute mission to not only rebuild New York but to keep America safe.

titre: Remarks at the Kent State Student Recreation Center in Kent, Ohio
texte: That's what I did for eight years as a senator.

titre: Remarks at the Kent State Student Recreation Center in Kent, Ohio
texte: I never stopped fighting to keep our country safer and to ensure that first responders got the medical care they needed.

titre: Remarks at the Kent State Student Recreation Center in Kent, Ohio
texte: And I think it's important to reflect on what each of us has done in moments like that.

texte: Because a lot of the crises that come at a president are not predicted.

texte: I'll tell you a quick story.

titre: Remarks at the Kent State Student Recreation Center in Kent, Ohio

titre: Remarks at the Kent State Student Recreation Center in Kent, Ohio

titre: Remarks at the Kent State Student Recreation Center in Kent, Ohio
texte: You learn a lot about people in moments like that.

texte: We made the decision to go forward, obviously.

texte: But we also did everything we could to double our efforts to find out about the intelligence and to secure the hundreds of thousands of people who would be there.

titre: Remarks at the Kent State Student Recreation Center in Kent, Ohio
texte: So you have to ask yourself: in a crisis, who would you trust?

titre: Remarks at the Kent State Student Recreation Center in Kent, Ohio
